live.prediction_time: Publication of the monthly Boletim Mensal de Seguranca de Barragens de Mineracao for reference month M. Each bulletin states its reference window explicitly ('Os dados analisados neste boletim referem-se as atualizacoes ocorridas entre 01/10/2026 e 01/11/2026') and is published 4-7 days after the window closes (archive page: Outubro 2026 published 05/11/2026 12h45; Setembro 2026 published 06/10/2026). At the instant the predictor knows: the full per-dam level lists as of 01/(M+1) (bulletin tables 5-8), the month-M transition table (bulletin table 4: dams with level changed during M, previous -> current, no per-dam event dates), and registry attributes. The target month M+2 opens at 01/(M+2), strictly after the instant; the M+1 intermediate month is skipped because its transition table is not yet published and its table cannot be split into before/after-instant events (no dated events) - see notes.md 'timing' for the dated example. Timezone: America/Sao_Paulo (federal publications carry no timezone; declared Brazilia time).

live.target: Binary: 1 if the port's Travellers Flow cell at ANY hourly snapshot in (T, T+24h] exceeds the CBSA highway-traveller service standard; 0 if no valid traveller cell in the window exceeds it. Threshold rule: the publisher's own service standard, whose documented forms are 10 minutes on weekdays (Mon-Thu) and 20 minutes on weekends (Fri-Sun) and holidays for FY2014-15..FY2017-18, and from FY2018-19 additionally 'July to August: 20 minutes (7 days a week)' (all quoted from CBSA service-standard pages, current and Wayback-pinned, see measurements.service_standard_evolution). Construction picks ONE of: (a) era-correct full rule (needs the FY2010-11..FY2013-14 forms verified - named prerequisite; FY2014-15 back is verified), or (b) the era-stable core rule 10/20 weekday/weekend-holiday everywhere (conservative, verified FY2014-15..present), or (c) a fixed plain threshold (e.g. >20 min) if the standard-linked rule proves unstable. Valid label denominator: traveller cells whose value is a minute count or 'No delay' (dictionary: 'No delay' = five minutes or less). 'Closed' (outside operating hours), 'Not applicable' (business line unavailable) and 'Missed entry' (no wait recorded) are not outcomes: an (office, hour) whose whole target window has no valid traveller cell is ineligible and right-censored out, never imputed; eligibility is decided from information at T (the port's own status history) not from the outcome. In-hour duplicate rows (publisher-acknowledged) are collapsed by a deterministic rule fixed before scoring: label = exceedance of ANY reported value in the (office, hour) group ('any' semantics; a conservative choice for a warning-use task, robust to the measured duplicate conflict pattern).

live.prediction_time: Instant: 13:00 UTC on day D+1. Features are everything published by then with event time <= D: the complete detection archive through day D (daily file for D observed complete at 09:05 BRT on D+1; detections stream near-real-time at 10-minute granularity during day D), calendar, state/biome. Optional covariates also available at the instant: observed fire-risk grid for day D (NetCDF published ~03:32 server time on D+1) and INPE's forecast risk grids for D+1..D+3 (published on day D). Excluded as post-instant: every detection row with event time > D, and any current-year statistic that only becomes final later. As-of policy: each detection row carries its event timestamp (data_pas / data_hora_gmt); the archive is treated as an append-mostly observation log; LIMITATION (recorded): INPE regenerates archive files (2003-2017 files regenerated 2025-09-08; 2024 file regenerated 2025-06-06) and no historical file vintages are kept, so features are taken from the current archive under the policy that detection rows are immutable observations; construction pins file checksums and must re-fetch one fixed month after >=2 weeks to measure late-row churn before quoting any number.

live.target: Label: whether the application ever achieves registration - a standing (is_standing=TRUE) registered event in the trade-mark events table, cross-checked against the application table's gained_registration_status_date and current status. Retroactively expunged registrations (is_standing=FALSE - revocation that legally 'unhappened' the grant, per the dictionary's 'What is is_standing?' section) do NOT count as registered. Post-registration lifecycle (ceased/removed/expired after grant, non-use removal) does not change a positive label. Negative: application terminated before any registration (refused/rejected/withdrawn/lapsed pre-registration/not_filed/cancelled/voided/linked). Censored: applications with no registration and no pre-grant terminal event at the extract date (recent filings, or rare very slow prosecutions) - excluded by eligibility cutoff, never silently dropped. Label source columns (events, status, registration dates) are excluded from shipped features.

live.split_strategy: Temporal by issue year, all three windows contiguous and disjoint. Proposed: train 2008-2018 (storm-based polygons began Oct 2007), eval 2019-2021, holdout 2022-2024. Anchor measurements support capacity but window totals are computed at construction: measured 2013 = 1,832 warnings / 441 verified (24.1%) spread over 100 distinct days with >=1 verified warning; measured 2023 = 2,531 / 656 (25.9%) over 115 distinct days. Positives cluster by outbreak day, so the clustered count (100-115 independent positive days per measured year) is the figure that matters for window capacity, not the row count. Base-rate drift is a documented property of the source (warning POD peaked 2011, declined 2012-14, then recovered - WAF-D-23-0153), so multi-year windows and a drift note are required, not a single-year holdout.

measurements.extraction_cost_measured: Per gazette: 355-576 KB, live fetch 0.1-2.0 s (four editions measured). measurements.gazette_structure_2026_11_05: Every A&D edition has the same 9-section layout (contents page measured): 1.1 new applications / 1.2 variation applications / 2.1 new granted / 2.2 new refused / 2.3 variation granted / 2.4 variation refused / 3 Schedule 4 / 4.1 withdrawn / 4.2 grants not taken up / 5.1 notices of public inquiries to be held / 5.2 decisions taken at public inquiries / 5.3-5.4 transport manager inquiries / 6 operating centre reviews / 7.1 licences surrendered / 7.2 licences terminated / 8 licences revoked without public inquiry / 9 corrections. Each entry is prefaced by its reference number (e.g. OF2094843 SI ALEX ACOZMEI LTD, directors, registered address, operating centre + postcode, authorisation counts, transport manager where applicable).
hazards: Refusal grounds (e.g. financial standing) are NOT in the listing - good for ex-ante validity, but if most refusals are driven by grounds invisible at T the achievable ceiling may be low; the refusal-grounds distribution is measurable from decision documents at construction and must be reported with any score.

Section volume drift across eras: 2021 and 2026 editions parse identically, but 2013-2016 era layouts (and the pre-2016 page format that carried no PDF attachments) are unverified; the coverage ledger decides the usable window.
Weekly refusal counts swing (0 in the 2021 sample week, 4 in the 2026 sample week): per-window class counts need the aggregate, not extrapolation from two editions.
Withdrawal semantics: 4.1 withdrawals are applicant choices, not regulator decisions; the binary label choice (refused-only vs refused-or-withdrawn) is a pre-registered construction decision.

Repeat applicants and multi-licence operators (e.g. GT Transport Services with three licence numbers in one decision) create entity clustering; cluster-aware splits/bootstrap by applicant name-key are required.
PI notices mix application inquiries (S13/S14) with enforcement (S26): the application-outcome population must filter by ground code, measured present in the notice text.

The gazette is a statutory public notice containing named individuals (directors, transport managers, drivers); construction should decide pseudonymisation of person names before any release (operator/centre fields are business data, cqc precedent for provider data).

records.question: At Alberta Wildfire's recorded initial assessment of a newly discovered wildfire (assessment_datetime, 'originally assessed'), predict whether the wildfire will escape initial attack - final area burned at least 100 ha (variants at 4/40/200 ha) - and/or remain uncontained more than 72 hours (time from assessment to first under control), using only the crew-observed assessment record (size at assessment, rate of spread, fire behaviour type, position on slope, in-situ weather over the fire, FBP fuel type), pre-instant timing fields (estimated ignition, reported, detection channel), and calendar/geography. A useful prediction supports the actual initial-attack resourcing decision - airtanker/crew prioritization and same-day escalation - which the agency itself states happens at this instant.
records.review: All five discovery contracts reconciled against recorded evidence (probes and full transcripts in candidates/ab-wildfire-ia-escape/). (1) Redistribution: class A - OGL-Alberta v2.2 permits redistribution and derivatives; the attribution sentence and non-endorsement wording are recorded verbatim and carried into LICENSE.md; the personal-information exemption was checked against the shipped columns (position codes, not names). (2) Prediction timing: the instant is the publisher's own initial-assessment timestamp and every intended feature is documented 'at the time of initial assessment' by the publisher's dictionary - the strongest timing documentation of any source this bench has opened; post-instant families (cause, dispatch, suppression milestones) are excluded with measured ordering evidence; declared limitations: no timezone marker in timestamps (read as America/Edmonton, assumption to confirm) and a single current compilation (no historical per-fire vintages) - the task is labelled current-compilation retrospective, and evaluation_contract must state these assumptions plus the bounded revision-flip exposure (89 fires within +-20% of 100 ha). (3) Target: labels derive from the record's own post-instant fields (current_size, first_uc_date), excludable from shipped features; eligibility is assessment-based with 100% coverage - no outcome-conditioned selection; no censoring (terminal status on every row, 99.9% extinguished). (4) Split capacity: three disjoint year windows carry both classes for both labels (escape 1.86%/1.85%/4.11%; containment 3.2%/3.4%/9.8%), with same-day clustered counts recorded (independence scale = the extreme fire-weather day); the holdout's higher rate is the documented 2023 record season. (5) Not a mirror: the IA-escape family is precedented (WildfireIA US benchmark, Mesogeos, Zong et al. Alberta powerline subset, Korkola et al. Ontario, UAlberta IA-difficulty study) - none ships an all-cause, assessment-instant task on the regulator's own in-situ assessment observations with containment-milestone labels; WildfireIA's own abstract records that such 'response records' are non-public in the US, which is precisely the gap this source closes for a public jurisdiction. Novelty verdict 'differentiated' recorded by script. Residual uncertainties for construction: confirm the timezone reading against a publicly documented fire timeline; decide the already-controlled stratum's treatment for the containment label; winter/season scope decision.

records.target: Primary label, binary: escape = final area burned (current_size, the publisher's 'final area burned of the wildfire') at or above the threshold (primary 100 ha; variants 4/40/200 ha measured). Secondary label, binary: containment = first under control (first_uc_date, 'sufficient suppression action to ensure no further spread') later than 72 hours after assessment_datetime; 42.0% of fires were already under control at the assessment instant (assessment == first_uc, a degenerate label-0 stratum the construction decision must handle and declare). Both labels derive entirely from the record's own post-instant fields; both source columns are excludable from what ships. Population: all wildfires in Alberta's Forest Protection Area, 2006-2025, one row per wildfire ((YEAR, FIRE_NUMBER) unique, measured); eligibility is assessment-based, not outcome-based (100% of discovered wildfires are assessed).

vintage_caveats: AIS datasets are 'updated weekly' (ACNC download page) and the register 'regularly updated': the files fetched 2026-10-31 are one vintage per year, not archived snapshots; a construction snapshot date must be pinned and recorded. The 2023->2024 trickle is measured (+1,234 post-census rows via the Charities Report cross-check)

Withheld records are removed 'from the date of approval onwards' (ACNC register page): a charity that lodged on time but later won withholding would show as absent -> false positive. Mechanism recorded; rate not measurable from the current files; direction bounded (can only add positives, never remove them). publicdata.au rehosts the register dataset with version history (HF 'National-Digital/acnc-register' card) - a possible historical-vintage channel for register attributes, unverified for the AIS files

'registration status' on historical rows is current-vintage (status as of the last weekly update), not status-at-lodgment; using it for eligibility must be done at construction under the prediction-contract gate (a 'Voluntarily Revoked*' exclusion is post-hoc and must be declared; a 'Revoked Double Defaulter' exclusion would remove true positives and must not be used as an exclusion)

records.prediction_time: Per-charity instant T = (the publisher-recorded 'ais due date' for the charity's period-Y AIS) minus 90 days. The due date is fixed by policy at six months after the reporting-period end (ACNC due-dates page), with the Commissioner's standing extension for standard 1 July-30 June periods to the following 31 January recorded in-file (measured: period ends 30/06/2023 carry due date 31/01/2024; 31/12/2024 carry 30/06/2025). Eligibility: the charity's period-(Y-1) AIS row exists with 'date ais received' <= T, and the charity is not listed as a member of an ACNC reporting group for period Y (group members lodge via their head entity; measured 2024: only 5 of 1,315 group-member ABNs also carry an individual period-2024 AIS row). All features come from the period-(Y-1) and earlier AIS datasets (finances, staffing, charity size, reporting-period structure, past lodgment timing including prior lateness) and the ACNC Register dataset; the target period-Y 'date ais received' (and row absence) is the label source and is excluded from features. Example instant (Australia/Sydney, AEDT): T = 2 November 2024 for a charity with FY ending 30/06/2024 (due 31/01/2025).

records.question: For an Australian charity registered with the ACNC that lodged its Annual Information Statement (AIS) for the reporting period ending in year Y-1 early enough that the lodgment was already recorded 90 days before its next deadline, will the charity FAIL to lodge its period-Y AIS by the ACNC-recorded due date for that period (the AIS 'date ais received' falls after the 'ais due date', or the charity never lodges a period-Y AIS and no row exists in the period-Y AIS dataset)?
records.review: Five contracts reconciled on measured evidence. (1) Redistribution: every input dataset carries an explicit CC BY licence (per-year variants recorded) - class A; attribution conditions carried to LICENSE.md. (2) Prediction timing: per-charity instant T = recorded due date - 90 days, example worked in Australia/Sydney with real timestamps (Integricare: T 02/11/2024, due 31/01/2025, received 03/02/2025); features are prior-period AIS content whose lodgment (hence observability) predates T by the eligibility rule; label columns excluded; vintage caveats (weekly updates, withheld-record removal, current-vintage status) recorded with the measured trickle and the bounded direction of the withheld channel - the as-of policy is current-vintage retrospective with pinned snapshot dates, to be probed at construction per the prediction-contract gate. (3) Target: publisher-recorded ('date ais received' vs 'ais due date' + absence), matching the ACNC's own KPI definition; censoring channels are publisher-coded (voluntary revocation status codes, group-membership files) and the residual mixture is measured (812 'Registered'-status absentees of 1,935 in 2023->2024) and declared part of the definition. (4) Split capacity: measured eligible-frame counts for disjoint windows train 2020-2021 (77,357 rows, 30.00% positive), eval 2022-2023 (80,977, 25.88%), holdout 2024 (42,885, 25.73%), both classes everywhere, positives spread over tens of thousands of charities. (5) Not a mirror: mechanical novelty search recorded; no ML-ready formulation of this or a sibling target exists externally; internal siblings target different outcomes (filing-population exit) in other jurisdictions. Uncertainty that remains: the withheld-record false-positive rate is unmeasured (mechanism recorded, direction bounded) and the 2013-2018 XLSX backfill for a longer train window is untested - both are construction-time, non-blocking.

records.split_strategy: Temporal windows on the target reporting-period year Y (periods ending in that calendar year; windows disjoint by Y). Candidate partition measured on the eligibility frame (prior AIS received <= T, group members excluded in construction): train Y in {2020, 2021}: 77,357 eligible rows / 23,205 positives (30.0%) / 54,152 negatives; eval {2022, 2023}: 80,977 / 20,958 (25.9%) / 60,019; holdout {2024}: 42,885 / 11,035 (25.7%) / 31,850. Both classes present in every window and every single year (per-year positive rates 25.7%-31.0%). Positives are spread across tens of thousands of distinct charities per year (eligible frames 37,970-42,885), not event clusters; a charity can appear in multiple target years, so per-charity clustering is a documented property for interval construction. XLSX-only years 2013-2018 can extend the train window at construction (worker parses XLSX; schema differences documented).
records.target: Binary label 1 = charity fails to lodge its period-Y AIS by the due date, computed from the publisher's own recorded fields in the period-Y AIS dataset: label 1 iff ('date ais received' > 'ais due date') OR (no row for the ABN in the period-Y dataset as of the snapshot). Label 0 iff 'date ais received' <= 'ais due date'. Label source columns: 'date ais received' and row presence (both excluded from shipped features; 'ais due date' is a legitimate feature because it is determined by the period end and announced deadline policy, known before T). The label matches the ACNC's own compliance KPI ('Percentage of ... Annual Information Statements submitted by the due date', Annual Report 2025-26 KPI 1.3: 76% for 2025, 73% for 2024) against measured on-time shares of 73.96% (2023 file) and 74.95% (2024 file).

measurements.vintage_caveats_2026_10_28: Finance's statistics page: 'Contract data can be amended, varied and updated by entities over time.' OCP registry quality notes: cancelled amendments overwrite status/period/value in OCDS compilations; item identifiers differ between original and amendment rows; supplier renames create duplicate supplier parties. Consequence recorded for construction: labels must be derived from amendment NOTICE rows (events), never from compiled/overwritten contract properties, and the FY/report files must be pinned by sha256 at harvest. The report and FY channels are publication-stream snapshots (each row a notice as published), so event rows are as-of honest; corrections/deletions of already-published notices cannot be ruled out for the most recent window and the holdout cutoff must keep a documented tail. GaPS-sourced rows (1999-2006-07, different schema) are excluded from the task era.

(1) Redistribution: SUPPORTED - licence class A, CC BY 3.0 AU quoted from AusTender's own Terms of Use clause 5.1 (contract notices are not ATM material), attribution statement clause 6.1 recorded for LICENSE.md; data.gov.au dataset licence cc-by corroborates; third parties commercially republish under the same grant. records.split_strategy: Temporal by parent publish date, all windows with both classes by construction from measured rates and volumes: train 2014-07-01..2018-06-30 (FY CSVs on data.gov.au; 60,590 parents in FY2017-18 alone, 110 agencies), eval 2018-07-01..2022-06-30 (data.gov.au FY files 2018-19/2019-20 + CnAndAmendmentsDownload windows for 2020-21..2021-22), holdout 2022-07-01..2025-09-30 (CnAndAmendmentsDownload windows + weekly export; every parent's 12-month label window closes by 2026-09-30, before the current data edge 2026-10-28). Measured basis (Jul-2017 cohort, n=6,285 parents published 01-31 Jul 2017, follow-up through 31-Jul-2018): first-amendment within 30d 0.38% / 90d 2.39% / 180d 5.62% / 365d 10.96% (689 positives in the cohort month). At ~5-6k parents/month and ~11% per year, each multi-year window carries tens of thousands of positives; per-window exact counts are the FIRST construction measurement on the worker (measured sample here, not extrapolated to a claimed total). Independence: contracts cluster by agency and publication month, so intervals must be clustered on (agency, publish-month); the independence scale is the publication month, not the row. Both channels (FY CSVs, amendments report) describe the same publication stream and cross-check each other; construction asserts channel-consistency in-build on overlapping windows.
records.target: Binary: 1 if any Contract Notice with Parent Contract ID == this CN ID (equivalently CN ID == '<parent>-A<n>' per the publisher's documented convention) is published with Amendment Publish Date in (T, T+365d]; 0 otherwise. The label source columns are the parent/amendment linkage, Contract Notice Type and Amendment Publish Date - all excluded from shipped features (only parent-row fields plus strictly-earlier aggregates ship). Amendments of every published reason (value increase, end-date extension, supplier change, cancellation) count as events; the 'Amendment Reason' field allows construction to state and test reason-specific variants. Censoring: parents whose 12-month window extends past the data cutoff are excluded, not imputed (live-edge rows counted per window).

The label is a later state change of the same notice: the publisher's data dictionary defines tenderStatus as 'A status that indicates whether a tender is Open (ie: accepting bids), Expired (no longer accepting bids) or Cancelled', and the publisher's support page states the files 'will include information on new, open, cancelled and expired notices that are published on the CanadaBuys website' and that 'Tender notice closing times will be displayed in Universal Time Coordinated minus 5 hours (UTC-0500)'. As-of policy: the open-data files re-state the CURRENT status of each notice (the complete file carries live Open rows; the closed-FY files carry only terminal statuses - measured FY2023-24 file: 6,414 Expired / 415 Cancelled, zero Open). Historical cancellation DATES are not published in the bulk files, so labels are read as terminal states from an archive snapshot pinned by sha256 at harvest; still-Open solicitations are censored (excluded, not imputed). Cancellation is operationally observable in real time on the CanadaBuys site and the files refresh at least daily (2026-2027 tender file Last-Modified measured Sat, 31 Oct 2026 10:30:31 GMT). Residual limitation, recorded not resolved: rare late reversions of already-published statuses cannot be excluded for the most recent window; construction runs a bounded notice-page verification on a sample of Cancelled rows.

records.question: For a Government of Canada competitive solicitation (noticeType in the RFP-like set: Request for Proposal, RFP against Supply Arrangement, Request for Standing Offer, Request for Supply Arrangement, Invitation to Qualify) whose original tender notice is published on CanadaBuys at instant T (publicationDate of the original notice row), will the solicitation be cancelled before award - i.e. its terminal tenderStatus is 'Cancelled' rather than 'Expired'? Features are the original-notice fields fixed at T: title and description text, contracting entity and its city/province, GSIN/UNSPSC and descriptions, procurement category, procurement method, selection criteria, trade agreements, regions of opportunity and delivery, expected contract start/end dates, and the closing date (documented UTC-0500) which with publicationDate gives the posting duration.
records.review: Five contracts at probe time: (1) Redistribution - SUPPORTED: OGL-Canada 2.0, explicit copy/modify/publish/adapt/distribute grant incl. commercial use, attribution statement required and carried to LICENSE.md; class A. (2) Prediction timing - SUPPORTED with recorded limitation: instant = original-notice publicationDate; every shipped feature is an original-notice field documented in the publisher's own data dictionary; the label is a post-instant terminal state from the publisher's own refreshed archive; cancellation dates are not in the bulk data, so the as-of policy is pinned-archive terminal-state with Open-row censoring + bounded notice-page verification at construction (weaker than dated-event labels like austender's; recorded as such). (3) Target - SUPPORTED: tenderStatus is a publisher-maintained column with documented three-value semantics; 'Expired' is observed absence (closed normally), 'Cancelled' the event; label column excludable; eligibility defined from information at the instant (notice type, competitive methods) not from outcomes. (4) Split capacity - PARTIALLY MEASURED: whole-FY2023-24 measured (5,749 eligible, 397 positives, 6.90%); legacy archive measured to carry the label across 2012-2022 via bounded slices; per-window exact counts need one bulk worker pass (recorded as the prerequisite to ready; never extrapolated to a claimed total). (5) Not a mirror - differentiated (novelty check recorded): no ML-ready cancellation task for any jurisdiction found; EU TED outcome-prediction literature studies different targets on a different jurisdiction and is not shipped ML-ready; the nearest bench sibling austender-contract-amendment-occurrence is the same domain but a different task contract (post-award contract amendments vs pre-award solicitation cancellation; different instant, population and label source).

records.target: Binary: 1 if the solicitation's terminal tenderStatus (current archive) is 'Cancelled'; 0 if 'Expired'. Multi-row rule: 499/6,829 FY2023-24 solicitations carry amendment rows with their own later publication dates, and 144 of those show differing statuses across rows - construction defines precedence as any-row-Cancelled (solicitation-level label), verified on a bounded sample against the notice pages; measured FY2023-24 impact of the precedence choice is small (base rate 6.08% under max-amendment-row vs 6.1-6.9% band). records.split_strategy: Temporal thirds on the frozen hourly archive 2010-01..2020-03, instant = snapshot hour; candidate windows train 2010-01..2016-12 / eval 2017-01..2018-12 / holdout 2019-01..2020-03 (each multi-year, disjoint, ordered; the 2020-03-21 COVID closure sits in the holdout's last 10 days and is a known-event fixture, not a whole-window effect). Clustering: (port, calendar-day) is the dependence unit (within-port serial correlation plus day-level demand shocks such as long weekends); clustered counts reported beside raw counts. Both classes expected in every window from measured per-port rates (12 ports with >30-min traveller exceedances in 2019 Q3 alone; 0 of 12 named busiest ports is all-negative), but exact per-window label counts at the chosen threshold rule are the FIRST construction measurement on the worker - the ~190 MB full archive is bulk work and stays off the coordinator; no sampled number is claimed as a total.
records.target: Binary: 1 if the port's Travellers Flow cell at ANY hourly snapshot in (T, T+24h] exceeds the CBSA highway-traveller service standard; 0 if no valid traveller cell in the window exceeds it. Label source: the Travellers Flow cells of the target window's snapshots; they are excluded from solver-visible features by a common-cutoff design (no shipped row may expose another scored row's outcome - the abs-visitor/canadabuys blind-join defect class is a named gate check). Threshold rule: the publisher's own service standard, whose documented forms are 10 minutes on weekdays (Mon-Thu) and 20 minutes on weekends (Fri-Sun) and holidays for FY2014-15..FY2017-18, and from FY2018-19 additionally 'July to August: 20 minutes (7 days a week)' (all quoted from CBSA service-standard pages, current and Wayback-pinned, see measurements.service_standard_evolution). Construction picks ONE of: (a) era-correct full rule (needs the FY2010-11..FY2013-14 forms verified - named prerequisite; FY2014-15 back is verified), or (b) the era-stable core rule 10/20 weekday/weekend-holiday everywhere (conservative, verified FY2014-15..present), or (c) a fixed plain threshold (e.g. >20 min) if the standard-linked rule proves unstable. Valid label denominator: traveller cells whose value is a minute count or 'No delay' (dictionary: 'No delay' = five minutes or less). 'Closed' (outside operating hours), 'Not applicable' (business line unavailable) and 'Missed entry' (no wait recorded) are not outcomes: an (office, hour) whose whole target window has no valid traveller cell is ineligible and right-censored out, never imputed; eligibility is decided from information at T (the port's own status history) not from the outcome. In-hour duplicate rows (publisher-acknowledged) are collapsed by a deterministic rule fixed before scoring: label = exceedance of ANY reported value in the (office, hour) group ('any' semantics; a conservative choice for a warning-use task, robust to the measured duplicate conflict pattern).

signoff.baseline_decision_criterion: Runner-contract model eval AUC on the identical 11,791 eval rows vs the unspsc_only reference bar 0.5707 (measured post-acceptance by the build's score.py, to be re-measured independently in the baseline job from the same bytes). Decision basis: the paired difference on identical rows with a publication-day-clustered bootstrap interval (the day is the gate's independence unit); headroom is demonstrated only if the model exceeds the bar and the clustered interval excludes zero. If the model trails the bar or the interval contains zero, record no demonstrated headroom under this protocol.
signoff.decision: RESOLVED - the assisted review is closed by rebuild cl-tender-003; artifact 27e610ba65e13805 is the accepted evidence base and the baseline decision may proceed on it.
reasoning: Finding 3 (label aggregation without a defined terminal state/horizon): repaired and measured. The label is now a deterministic function of a closed, vintage-covered window: award releases dated inside pub+180d are walked in date order and the last terminal status decides (active->adjudicated=0, all-unsuccessful->deserted=1, all-cancelled->revoked); pending is non-terminal; the compiledRelease fallback is dropped and bucketed. HORIZON_DAYS=180 was frozen from measured first-award-release lags (p50 33-41 d, p90 <=102 d) and capped by the zip vintages (holdout latest release 2021-12-30 >= 2021-06-30+180d = 2021-12-27), so 180 d is the maximum uniform horizon the source supports and no split's labels depend on data its vintage lacks. mixed_terminal 0 and duplicate_ocid 0 in every split; awardUpdate-tagged releases are matched (the previous exact-tag filter silently ignored them - caught by the synthetic smoke before worker spend).

Finding 1 (cancelled awards assigned no target, blank targets silently removed): repaired by declaration and measurement. Revoked and right-censored rows are named, counted buckets per split - revoked_rate 0.0286/0.0444/0.0383, censored_rate 0.0453/0.0566/0.0512, scored_share 0.9262/0.8990/0.9105 (train/eval/holdout) - with the unobserved-target decomposition (no_award_within_horizon / award_beyond_horizon / pending_within_horizon) counted from the rows, never inferred. No row leaves the scored files silently.

Finding 2 (selection declared as publication-time-only while actually conditioned on the outcome): repaired by making the declaration true. Membership is decided by publication-time fields only (first tender release month + publication state 'active' + ocid). The scored CSVs are explicitly declared as the OUTCOME-DEPENDENT subset of that membership in quality.json's row_selection basis, which requires the outcome_conditioning rates to be quoted beside any score taken from this artifact. The reopen condition's first clause is satisfied at the membership level; the scored-subset restriction itself cannot be made publication-time-decidable because the outcome is genuinely future, so the review closes on the qualification skill's alternative path: the intended population and observation mechanism are resolved explicitly (fixed horizon, measured per-split rates) instead of being hidden behind a timing-neutral claim.

Scientific acceptability of the conditional population: the prediction instant (publication; features are administrative records written then) strictly precedes the label window (<= pub+180d). Conditioning the task population on reaching an observed terminal state within a fixed horizon is a competing-risks-style conditional prediction task, legitimate when declared with measured rates; the defect the review caught was the false publication-time claim plus the ill-defined any-active label, both now gone. The conditioning is uniform across splits (scored_share 0.90-0.93 everywhere, applied by one rule), so eval/holdout comparisons are not differentially distorted by it; the residual prevalence shift (holdout 25.1% vs train 17.6%) stays documented as a property, and the fixed-horizon rule also avoids the 'terminal at today's snapshot' failure mode - no label depends on when the data was downloaded.
signoff.scope_limitation: Every score from this artifact describes the conditional population only: tenders whose process reaches a terminal adjudicated-or-deserted state within 180 days of publication (~90-93% of eligible rows per split). Deployment over all published tenders would face the excluded revoked (~3-4%) and unresolved-at-180d (~5%) cases this task does not score. Any card or report quoting a score must quote the outcome_conditioning rates beside it (this requirement is written into the accepted quality.json row_selection basis).

records.prediction_time: The instant is a fetch of CONAGUA SIH's per-dam historical CSV after its weekly update (publisher statement, SIH homepage: 'La actualizacion de los archivos se realiza semanalmente' - files are updated weekly). T is the latest Fecha row present in the file at fetch. Observed 2026-10-27: the Cuchillo, La Amistad, Falcon, Solis and Infiernillo files each carried rows through 2026-10-26 (T = yesterday); one sampled dam (LDCVC) lagged at 2026-09-28, so T is measured per dam per fetch. All feature rows are Fecha <= T; every target row is Fecha in (T, T+30]. The SIH files are the publisher's cumulative current-vintage archive, not point-in-time snapshots: the portal warns 'Algunas bases de datos pueden incluir actualizaciones retroactivos por lo que la informacion historica puede cambiar en actualizaciones posteriores', and the 1990s show partial backfill (ALRBN volume column 50 percent populated 1990-1999, 100 percent from 2000). Features are therefore stated as current-vintage values, same treatment as the published abs-visitor-arrivals-direction record; no claim of historical operational availability is made (see review). The daily observation cutoff time within a day is not documented by the publisher; the contract uses whole calendar days (America/Mexico_City), features <= T, target > T, so no intra-day ordering is assumed.
records.publisher: Comision Nacional del Agua (CONAGUA), Gobierno de Mexico
records.question: For a Mexican dam in the CONAGUA SIH reservoir network (210 catalogued dams, 26 states) whose published stored volume VolumenAlm on the latest available day T is at or above the drought threshold (25 percent of the dam's reference capacity), will VolumenAlm fall below that threshold on at least one day in the 30 calendar days after T (a drought-onset event)? A useful prediction supports water-allocation planning, drought-monitoring inputs (the official Monitor de Sequia en Mexico uses reservoir availability as an index), and urban supply outlooks (Monterrey 2022, Tijuana 2019-2022, Falcon 2002 crises all crossed this threshold in this panel).
records.review: Five contracts, reconciled against written evidence: (1) Redistribution SUPPORTED - CC BY 4.0 on the publisher's own resource record (class A), quoted with URL; attribution 'CONAGUA, SIH' carried into LICENSE.md at release. (2) Prediction timing SUPPORTED with documented vintage limitation - the instant is stateable and observed (weekly-updated file; T = latest Fecha, measured 2026-10-26 on a 2026-10-27 fetch; one sampled dam lagged 29 days, so T is measured per dam per fetch); every feature row is Fecha <= T, the whole target window is Fecha > T; current-vintage treatment documented because the publisher warns of retroactive updates and the archive is cumulative (partial 1990s backfill observed) - no historical operational-availability claim, which is what the evaluation contract must state. (3) Target SUPPORTED - label from VolumenAlm(Mm3) rows after T, excludable by date filter; eligibility defined only from information at T (>= 365 prior rows, volume at/above threshold); censoring: missing days recorded as absent rows (no fabricated zero volumes), and right-edge truncation only affects the last 30 days; threshold frame ambiguity identified and bounded - two frames measured, the proxy is the strictly harder threshold, so events under the proxy are a subset of events under the official-capacity frame and capacity holds under both. (4) Split capacity SUPPORTED - 26-dam stratified sample measured from the source: 357 onset events, 202/84/71 across train/eval/holdout, both classes in every window, 271 (dam, year) clusters recorded; the full-panel count is a worker measurement recorded as the first construction step (monotone in dams: additional dams cannot empty a window). (5) Not a mirror SUPPORTED - novelty check recorded with verdict differentiated: prior art ships raw series (ResOpsUS 679 US dams; GROWL 4,134 global series) or closed-data studies (Türkiye, data 'under official permission and commercial terms'); no ML-ready public dam-storage drought-onset prediction task with an as-of policy, splits and a scored contract exists for Mexico or any jurisdiction; this task shape was probed twice before on this bench (tw-reservoir-drought-storage, za-dws-dam-storage-exceedance) and both died on ACCESS, never sourcing the shape - this candidate sources it. Unresolved, recorded: full-panel split counts (worker prerequisite); official per-dam capacities need a proper parse of the weekly-report archive (the PDF text layer is scrambled); intra-day observation cutoff undocumented (contract avoids assuming one); the weekly-summary cell-level cross-check is deferred to construction with the press-figure corroboration standing in its place.

records.split_strategy: Dam-day panel, temporal windows on the prediction instant: candidate partition train T<=2010 / eval 2011-2018 / holdout 2019-2026 (all three windows observed to carry both classes in the 26-dam stratified sample: 202 / 84 / 71 onset events; construction recomputes on the full 210-dam panel, which is monotone - additional dams can only add events, never empty a window). Events cluster by dam-season: 357 events over 26 dams = 271 distinct (dam, year) clusters; clustered counts must be reported beside raw counts. Dams with zero historical onsets at the chosen threshold (4 of the 26 sampled) are an eligibility choice for construction: either exclude or keep as all-negative rows, decided and documented at build time.
records.target: Binary: 1 if VolumenAlm(Mm3) < threshold on at least one day with Fecha in (T, T+30] in the dam's SIH series, else 0. Label source column: VolumenAlm(Mm3) (the same column as the target variable), excluded from features by the Fecha <= T filter; no other column carries the answer. Threshold frame, two candidates measured in the sample: (a) discovery-time proxy = 25 percent of the dam's own observed maximum VolumenAlm (the SIH catalog carries no capacity column); (b) construction-time preferred frame = 25 percent of official capacity, published per dam in CONAGUA's weekly 'Almacenamiento de las Principales Presas del Pais' report (columns CAPACIDAD MUERTA / CAP. UTIL DISENO Mm3; archive at ftp://ftp.conagua.gob.mx/Gobmx/DisponibilidadenPresas/) and in the press-percentage frame (e.g. El Cuchillo capacity 1,123 Mm3 vs observed max 1,765.7 Mm3 including flood surcharge; the proxy threshold 441.4 Mm3 equals 39 percent of the official frame, so the proxy is the conservative/higher threshold and events under it are a subset of events under the official frame). Eligibility at T, from information available at prediction: dam has >= 365 prior daily VolumenAlm rows and VolumenAlm(T) >= threshold (onset formulation; days already below threshold are not prediction rows).

records.question: For a CPCB continuous ambient air-quality monitoring station in India, will the station's next-day (D+1) 24-hour mean PM2.5 concentration exceed 90 micrograms/m3 - the lower breakpoint of the CPCB National AQI 'Poor' band for 24-hour PM2.5 - given only that station's own hourly PM2.5 history through the end of day D?
records.review: Five contracts reconciled 2026-11-05 against recorded evidence. (1) REDISTRIBUTION - supported, class A: CPCB's own publication is licensed GODL-India by the data.gov.in platform instrument (Wayback-read 2026-11-04, AIKosh-corroborated live; attribution template + non-endorsement to carry into LICENSE.md; no share-alike); the XKDR compilation is CC BY 4.0 (README, credit 'India Air Quality Database, XKDR Forum' + CPCB + US DoS); OpenAQ is CC BY 4.0 (docs + archived v2 meta 'CC BY 4.0d'). (2) PREDICTION TIMING - supported for a clearly-labelled retrospective-research scope with two declared, unverified assumptions: instant = 23:59 IST on day D; features = the station's own trailing PM2.5 history through day D (naive IST, calendar-day convention); label = calendar-day D+1 24-hr mean, entirely after the instant. Assumption (a) current-vintage: the archive is one export (2026-09-30), values 'as reported', 'no gap filling', 'preliminary and not fully validated' (XKDR README) - no operational as-of claim; revision behaviour unmeasured (a second export has never been observed). Assumption (b) day-D trailing hours are treated as complete at the instant: CPCB intraday latency is not measured (the publisher's own 4 PM bulletin averages the past 24 h and shows non-participating stations, e.g. Delhi 36/39 on 2024-11-18). (3) TARGET - supported: mechanical label (D+1 calendar-day mean > 90 ug/m3) from a published band edge of the publisher's own AQI instrument (Poor band lower edge 91; quote in measurements.threshold_fixture_2026_11_05); label-source series excluded from every shipped column; known-event fixture bound to the publisher's Daily AQI Bulletin (2024-11-18 Delhi Severe 494) AND confirmed in the measured panel (36/36 complete Delhi station-days TRUE); the bulletin is also the publisher-summary cross-check (category-level). (4) SPLIT CAPACITY - supported, measured on the full 2019-2025 panel and re-cut once with measured evidence before any score (see split_strategy): train 2019-2022 63735 positives, eval 2023 20773 positives over 357 distinct positive days, holdout 2024 19254 positives over 358 days; both classes in all three windows; winter clustering recorded and cluster-aware evaluation required at construction. (5) NOT A MIRROR - supported: novelty_check verdict differentiated (2026-10-20): research papers fit CPCB forecasters with private splits (arXiv 2404.08702 22-station; Discover AI 2026), Kaggle raw-data mirrors (CC BY-SA), and open archives (OpenAQ/XKDR/Vayuayan) - none ships this task with fixed splits and a scored contract. RESIDUAL LIMITATIONS carried to construction: (i) the cross-row exposure - a scored day-D row's label operand (day D+1 mean) appears inside the trailing features of days D+2..D+91 - requires the za-cct-style bounded-exposure design (restricted trailing aggregates, isolated_rows declared, gate-1.5 reverse-history probes measuring eval/holdout coverage and mismatch); (ii) label-availability exclusions (station-days with <18 h on D+1) must be counted and declared, never silently dropped; (iii) the export's 2025 hole (Jan-Mar, Oct-Dec absent; the 2025-04..09 tail excluded) and the OpenAQ 2023-2024 gap (zero files, measured) mean XKDR is the only channel that carries all three re-cut windows; the full-key bulk path stays behind the operator's email/key decision while the anonymous measurements-API batching path remains viable and measured.

records.prediction_time: The T3010 filing deadline for the year-Y fiscal period: six months after the fiscal period end (documented on the publisher's T3010 form page: 'submit annually ... within six months of the end of its fiscal period'). At that instant everything the charity has ever filed (year-Y return and all earlier ones) is knowable, and the year-Y+1 outcome is not: returns for fiscal periods ending in Y+1 are not due until at least six months into Y+1, and the publisher's year-Y+1 list product appears later still. Features are therefore the year-Y and earlier returns only; every year-Y+1 field is the label source and never ships. MEASURED 2026-11-03 (publication lag + framing evidence, probe/out/probe_2026_11_03.json): the per-year List packages appear on open.canada.ca well after the FPE year - year-2023 package created 2025-07-29, year-2024 package created 2026-03-06 (both single-year creations that look like genuine first publication); the older packages were bulk-created (1990-2008 all 2026-02-20; 2009-2012 2021-11-29; 2013-2022 2024-12-17), so portal metadata dates do NOT evidence first publication for older years. Two honest framings therefore exist and ADVANCEMENT PICKS ONE AS ITS FIRST STEP (the cqc precedent): (a) deadline instant - the recorded instant; a retrospective filer-information scope with the explicit assumption that the year-Y return is filer-known but not yet third-party published at T (za-cct retrospective precedent, no operational third-party availability claim); (b) year-Y list publication instant - fully third-party operational (everything through FPE-Y is published), at the cost that some label events are already due by then (Jan-31-FPE charities' Y+1 returns are due before the Y-list appears), a partial-nowcast shape the abs/ocha-fts candidates already carry honestly. Label semantics are identical under both. Files carry '_updated' suffixes and packages are modified after creation (2024 package modified 2026-10-04), so labels are computed from current-vintage finalized files; no historical-vintage claim is made.

measurements.artifact_allowance_check_2026_11_05: PRE-COMPLETION CHECK (written 2026-11-05 19:2xZ, while dvsa-mot-build-001 was still running, BEFORE any outcome existed). The launched job declares max_artifact_mb = 8, and workers/upload.py refuses the WHOLE staging upload (reports included) when the bytes under /output plus source.tar plus container.log exceed that allowance. MEASURED inputs: 2024 source year = 7,667,648,876 B uncompressed (~64M rows at the prefix-measured ~120 B/row); first-4MB prefix of test_result_202408.csv = 34,924 rows with 19,328 distinct vehicle_ids; shipped extract = 21 plain-CSV columns. ESTIMATE (not a measurement): the md5 mod 1000 == 0 vehicle sample keeps ~0.1% of a multi-ten-million vehicle panel, so the pair panel plausibly lands in the hundreds-of-thousands of rows (~30-130 MB extract) - every other candidate in the catalog sized max_artifact_mb to its extract (austin 131 MB extract -> 400; msha 3.38 GB -> 4200; za-cct 8.4 MB -> 24), while this job's 8 MiB supports only ~60k rows at ~128 B/row. PREDICTION, not a finding: if the extract exceeds the allowance, publish() raises UploadError('Artifacts exceed job allowance') and NOTHING uploads - but executor.py still embeds /output/summary.json (<= 64 KiB) in /opt/scout/result.json and `worker collect` is designed to fetch exactly that, so the measured row counts, per-file sizes and the 19-file vintage sha256 pins survive for a correctly-sized rebuild. RESPONSE PRE-REGISTERED: one corrected rebuild (dvsa-mot-build-002, new job ID per the immutable-bundle rule) with max_artifact_mb sized from the collected per-file bytes with >= 2.5x headroom; construction logic unchanged - this is a job-descriptor defect, not a build defect; the gate/triad then rerun deterministically on the rebuilt bytes. If collect instead shows a clean upload, this entry is void and the baseline proceeds as recorded.

construction_preflight_2026_11_05.pre_registered_triad: Deciding members (written before any construction or score, mirrored in source/score.py): persistence_prior_result (the prior test's own initial-fail flag - the last observed outcome), calendar_make_week (train-estimated rate per make x ISO week-of-year, make then global fallback), vehicle_train_rate (train-estimated rate per vehicle_id - the panel identity prior). records.split_strategy: Temporal on the PREDICTION INSTANT (the prior completed class-4 test's date, the latest shipped knowable date): train priors 2009-01-01..2018-12-31, eval 2019-01-01..2021-12-31, holdout 2022-01-01..2023-11-30. CHANGED from the original next-test-year windows (train next-tests 2010-2018 / eval 2019-2021 / holdout 2022-2024) BEFORE any construction or score: the gate checks split windows against the declared time_column, and the next test's date is label-side timing information that cannot ship, so next-test-year windows are unverifiable from the rows; prior-year windows keep every check coherent with available data (label years shift ~+1, boundary lead-time overlap documented). Right-censoring cutoff: priors on/after 2023-12-01 are excluded wholesale (counted) so no row needs a next test beyond the 2024-12 data end - the excluded tail is exactly where short-gap post-failure retests would otherwise survive an annual-cycle censoring and bias prevalence. Population bounds (all pre-registered before any score): class 4 only (both sides of every pair; other classes counted and skipped), vehicles deterministically hash-sampled md5(vehicle_id) mod 1000 == 0 (~0.1%, outcome-independent, fixed before any split), completed tests only (ABR/ABA <0.6% measured - excluded from both sides and counted), pairs are consecutive completed class-4 tests in (test_date, completed_date, file order) after dedup of exact duplicate projected rows (test_id is NOT unique - measured 2026-10-19). Tests 2005-2008 are prior-history priming only. vehicle_id ships as a declared high-cardinality feature and is the event/cluster key; the runner id column is row_key (vehicle_id + pair ordinal, unique by construction).
records.target: Binary from the documented test_result field of the next test: positive if test_result is F or PRS - the DfT/DVSA documented 'initial failure' definition ('Initial failure rate = (Test Fail Results + Test PRS Results) / Total Tests', MOT Testing Data User Guide; the same definition drives the published DVSA/MOT/01 statistical tables). Negative if P. Abandoned/aborted codes (ABR, ABA - measured present at <0.6%) are excluded or handled at construction, to be decided and documented there.

measurements.api_contract_2026_10_19: LDA conventions learned from the API's own error text (each from a 400/404 that named the problem): regime segment is compliance-rBWD (not 'bwd'); the generic /compliance/... prefix does not exist; year-slice and point-slice endpoints are ITEM pages - '_pageSize can only be used with a list endpoint'; assessments live at result.primaryTopic.observation; '?year=...' is 'unrecognised short name or literal: year'.
measurements.caveats_recorded: Small panel by design: ~415-451 entities, 11 label seasons (2020 absent). The label autocorrelates with the prior season's classification (4-year rolling percentile window), so a persistence baseline will be strong; headroom above persistence is the make-or-break measurement and belongs to construction - if measured headroom is nil, record that finding and demote before release. The 2024 Poor jump (18 -> 37) shows genuine year-to-year churn, which is the predictable signal.
measurements.cross_check_against_published_summary_pr: At construction, cross-check per-season counts against the EA's published annual classification announcements and Swimfo's national percentages for the same seasons (the measured 2024/2025 Poor counts of 37/32 are the fixture to match).
measurements.in_season_slice_contract_2026_10_23: Re-measured today: the in-season point slice (.../in-season/slice/point/03600?_format=json) returns 849 observations whose only fields are `_about` and `sampleWeek` - there is NO bacterial result value in the published in-season records, so per-sample exceedance features cannot be built from this source. The season slice's compliance observation carries only the bathing-water link and the classification.
measurements.persistence_ceiling_2026_10_23: Pre-launch measurement on the publisher's ten season slices (2015-2025, 2020 suspended), command `python3 candidates/ea-bathing-water-classification/eab_ceiling.py`, report ceiling-2026-10-23.json in this directory. Not a qualification report: no gate ran, no model was fitted. Panel 3,359 rows; frame 2016-2019 / 2022-2023 / 2024-2025 (2015 has no 2014 slice and 2021's Y-1 season 2020 does not exist: 878 water-seasons without a prior observation, 17 Closed labels excluded). Rows/positives/rate: train 1,652/121/0.0732, eval 836/71/0.0849, holdout 871/102/0.1171. Binary persistence AUC 0.850/0.820/0.940; ORDINAL persistence AUC (last season's published 4-level classification) 0.951/0.958/0.981; 3-season count reference 0.859/0.847/0.941; majority-class accuracy 0.927/0.915/0.883. Transitions 2022+: 1511 stay-negative, 138 stay-positive, 35 onset, 23 recovery. Positive waters per split 50/44/67.
measurements.sample_grain_2026_10_19: In-season point slice for point 05300 (South Shields): 794 sample observations back to 1988 (first item: sample 1988-05-11 14:40, week 1988-W19) - per-sample records exist through the API for feature history.
measurements.season_counts_2026_10_19: Measured via 11 season-slice requests (each ~230 KB, <1 s, ~2.5 MB total - the panel itself needs no worker): 2015: 415 (E 264 / G 109 / S 29 / P 11 / Closed 2); 2016: 415 (287/98/22/6/2); 2018: 422 (282/106/23/9/2); 2022: 421 (302/87/18/12/2); 2023: 424 (281/99/25/18/1); 2024: 451 (289/95/29/37/1); 2025: 451 (297/95/25/32/2). review.finding: Persistence dominates the candidate's own information set. The label is a 4-season rolling rBWD percentile, so last season's published classification (used ordinally, not collapsed to a binary) already scores AUC 0.958 on eval and 0.981 on holdout. The apparent gap against binary persistence (0.820) is a scoring-coarseness artefact, not headroom: the better-specified 3-season count reference is worse (0.847/0.941). Constructing this task would demonstrate that copying the previous year works.
review.scope_limits: Pre-launch ceiling on published slices - no gate, no accepted artifact and no fitted model, so this is not the skill's model-vs-persistence measurement and does not establish that no model can exceed 0.958 by a small margin. The publisher's in-season records carry no result values (measured), so the re-scope this design would need cannot come from this source.

records.split_strategy: Temporal by reporting cycle: train on early-cycle transitions, eval on middle cycles, holdout on the newest public cycles (2021-2022 provisional / 2022-2023 final at the far end). Both classes are present in every measured cycle window (2023 call: 11.2% positives, 21,537 answered plants, 30 reporters). MEASURED CAVEAT: only the 2022-2023 cycle was downloaded and measured this session (2,411 positives); the 2011-2012, 2021-2022 and any recoverable 2007-2020 cycles are confirmed public only by catalogue/share-link HEAD probes, not by row counts - construction step 1 is to pin the public cycle inventory and measure the uwwCode join rate between at least two cycles. Positives cluster by country reporting regime (measured: any-F rate DE 0.4% vs NO 49.6%), so clustered/stratified counts per split must be reported; a split that puts a country's plants only in train and only in eval would measure regime shift, not plant performance.
records.target: Binary from the source row of cycle N+1: label = 1 iff the plant (uwwState=1, active) has at least one treatment-performance parameter assessed 'F' among the six uww*Perf fields, restricted to plants with at least one answered (P or F) parameter; plants with only NA/NR/blank assessments are unobserved-target rows, counted separately, never dropped silently. Measured on the full 2023 call CSV: 2,411 positives / 21,537 answered (11.2% base rate). The uww*Perf codes are P/F/NA/NR (documented in the Eionet data dictionary element pages, e.g. element 104947 'Treatment performance: BOD5'); the 'In cause of failure' fields (uwwBadPerformance 'Bad performance' 1,765 Yes among active, uwwBadDesign 'Bad design or dimensioning', uwwAccidents 'Major accidents', uwwInformation free text) describe the reported CAUSE where the plant does not meet requirements and are label-source/label-adjacent columns, excluded from features. IMPORTANT measured property recorded as part of the definition: the label is 'REPORTED as failing' - a mixture of physical performance and the national reporting regime; measured 2023-call any-F rates range from DE 0.4% (16/3,776) and BE 2.8% to NO 49.6% (116/234), HR 53.5% (46/86) and RO 36.3% (352/971). Country is therefore a legitimate feature AND the reference baseline must be country-stratified; the mixture is the task's documented semantics, not a defect to hide.

Removal mixes automatic removal for a missed compulsory annual update (documented rule: deadline one year after registration and then one year after each annual update; missed deadline -> suspended, then 'automatically removed two weeks after the deadline'), voluntary deregistration, and rare enforcement removals; the publisher's own mapping report counts '87% complying timely ... and 1 496 registrants removed' for its reporting period. records.split_strategy: Temporal at installation-year grain, one row per (installation, compliance year t): train t <= 2019 (2005-2019), eval 2020-2022, holdout 2023-2025, all restricted to in-frame installation-years (both VERIFIED_EMISSIONS and ALLOCATION numeric). Measured on the 2026-10-20 snapshot (measured_net_short_by_year in notes.md): every year 2005-2025 carries both classes; eligible rows per year range 7,402 (2025) to 11,520 (2012); the net-short base rate drifts by phase - 27.7-31.3% in phase 1/2 (2005-2012), 56.4-71.5% in phase 3 (2013-2020), 69.8-80.6% in phase 4 (2021-2025) - a documented phenomenon property (free-allocation share fell and benchmarks tightened while the cap declined), the analogue of the flunet COVID-era base-rate break; construction must document it, not smooth it. Entities recur across windows by construction (23,708 installation keys observed over 2005-2030 rows), so the row id must be the composite (registry, installation, year) and the recurring-entity property declared, not mistaken for split leakage; positives cluster weakly at the installation level (an installation's net-short status is autocorrelated year to year), so the clustered count to report is distinct installations going net-short in a window, measured at construction.
records.target: Binary, computed from the source row of (installation, year t): VERIFIED_EMISSIONS(t) > ALLOCATION(t), where ALLOCATION is the free allocation recorded in the registry for year t and VERIFIED_EMISSIONS is the independently verified emissions figure. Unit: both are tonnes CO2-equivalent per installation-year (1 allowance = 1 tonne); the comparison is unit-free within the source's own frame (no external threshold or datum is involved). Frame restriction: installation-years where both VERIFIED_EMISSIONS and ALLOCATION are numeric ('n/a' rows - not-yet-operating, excluded or closed sites - are out of frame and their handling must be pinned at construction). Label source columns VERIFIED_EMISSIONS and ALLOCATION at year t are recorded in label_source_columns and must be absent from the shipped features; feature rows may use emissions/allocation/surrender values only for years <= t-1 plus year-t allocation.

records.prediction_time: The prediction instant is the lavratura instant: DAT_HORA_AUTO_INFRACAO of the current auto de infracao, the earliest documented moment the enforcement act exists (recorded by the electronic AI-e form since 2019-10-08, and by the launch date DT_LANCAMENTO for the pre-2019 analogue SICAFI series). Features are restricted to (a) the current auto's issuance-time attributes (infraction type/code, proposed sanction TIPO_AUTO, initial value VAL_AUTO_INFRACAO, gravity classification GRAVIDADE_INFRACAO, conduct MOTIVACAO_CONDUTA, UF/municipio, bioma, action motivation TIPO_ACAO, operation name) and (b) the entity's PRIOR autos only (DAT_HORA_AUTO_INFRACAO strictly earlier than the instant). Post-instant process events defined by IN Ibama 19/2023 (ciencia of the auto, defense, julgamento in first instance ~30 days from file receipt, appeal ~20 days, second instance, Cadin inclusion) are label-window events of the current auto's lifecycle, never features. LIMITATION, recorded: the daily export is current-vintage only (no publisher archive of past exports); prior-history features are therefore current-vintage rows with per-row DT_ULT_ALTERACAO / TP_ULT_ALTERACAO / JUSTIFICATIVA_ALTERACAO available to quantify how much history was revised. The 12-month target window follows the prediction instant entirely. MEASURED 2026-11-04 (worker probe ibama-probe-002, full current vintage, 705,667 rows): DAT_HORA_AUTO_INFRACAO is non-empty on 705,667/705,667 rows (91,632 date-only 'YYYY-MM-DD' concentrated in the pre-AIe eras + 614,035 full 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS'), so the lavratura instant is directly the published column on every row; the DT_LANCAMENTO fallback was never needed (0 rows fell back; DT_LANCAMENTO itself is empty on 479 rows); 0 unparseable dates. Every row carries the same export stamp 2026-11-03 01:28:15, i.e. the zip is one full daily re-export (current-vintage only). Revision churn measured from DT_ULT_ALTERACAO: rows altered within the 12 months before the export stamp are <=1.2% for every lavratura year <=2024, 30.5% for 2025 and 100% for 2026 - the current-vintage limitation is concentrated in the most recent ~18 months, matching the censoring design; the evaluation contract must state the retrospective/current-vintage as-of policy (datasus-sinasc precedent). Timestamps carry no timezone; treated as publisher-local (America/Sao_Paulo).

records.review: Five contracts, reconciled against written evidence (worker probe ibama-probe-002, full current vintage, 2026-11-04): (1) Redistribution SUPPORTED - class A per Decreto 8.777/2016 art. 2 III / art. 4 as amended by Decreto 9.903/2019 (permissive instruments quoted 2026-10-30 in licence_note and license_evidence), dataset marked 'Outra (Aberta)'; LGPD duty recorded: entity keys shipped hashed, NOME_INFRATOR never shipped. (2) Prediction timing SUPPORTED with documented vintage limitation - instant = lavratura, present on 705,667/705,667 rows (measured; DT_LANCAMENTO fallback unused); the zip is one full daily re-export (single stamp on all rows) and no publisher archive of past vintages exists, so the as-of policy is retrospective/current-vintage - revision churn measured at <=1.2%/yr for lavratura years <=2024, 30.5% for 2025, 100% for 2026, and the evaluation contract must state it (datasus-sinasc precedent); the 12-month target window lies strictly after the instant by construction. (3) Target SUPPORTED - mechanical same-table label (entity + strictly-later lavratura within 365 days), label source columns excludable, entity coverage 95.3% measured and cross-validated against the publisher's TP_PESSOA_INFRATOR column (exact match), right-censoring measured (2,347 rows of 2025, all 10,562 of 2026 inside the unobserved window); this is a re-AUTUACAO task under enforcement attention, not a reoffense claim - stated in the task card, not hidden. (4) Split capacity SUPPORTED, measured on the full table - every window carries both classes with thousands of independent clusters (train 44,805 positives over 23,430 entities / 6,149 actions; eval 18,216 over 8,573 / 13,624; holdout 14,995 over 7,241 / 14,800), so the clustered-positives gate cannot fail camara-style; base-rate drift 17.8% -> 27.7% -> 28.4% recorded as a phenomenon property. (5) Not a mirror SUPPORTED - differentiated novelty verdict recorded 2026-10-30 (mechanical check; prior art = causal survival analyses of flora subsets 2000-2010, no ML-ready benchmark with splits and a scored contract); the formulation is unchanged by this measurement and the recorded verdict stands. Cross-check against the publisher's own summary product done with a measured discrepancy recorded honestly (multas product distinct-AI ratios 1.02-1.20 pre-2020, 0.82-0.90 in the AIe era) - construction must define the population from the main table alone. Verdict: READY for construction handoff.

records.split_strategy: Entity-instant panel over all autos in the current vintage (1977-09-03..2026-10-30 measured): one row per (entity, auto) with prior-history features strictly earlier than the lavratura instant. MEASURED 2026-11-04 on the full current table (ibama-probe-002, zip sha256 4db188142b03a598d839f5331d3c148aeb7718fd6a657f324d8e98b959621771, 123,308,204 bytes, export stamp 2026-11-03 01:28:15; 705,667 rows, 0 duplicate SEQ in this export - the publisher's multiplicity warning did not materialize in the 2026-11-03 csv): windows on lavratura year, valid-entity, right-censored at 2025-10-30 23:59:59 - train 2005-2015: 251,614 rows / 44,805 positives (17.81%), 23,430 distinct positive entities, 6,149 distinct SEQ_ACAO_FISCALIZATORIA, 132 distinct (year,month), 27 UFs; eval 2016-2019: 65,725 / 18,216 (27.72%), 8,573 / 13,624 / 48 / 27; holdout 2022-2025: 52,741 / 14,995 (28.43%), 7,241 / 14,800 / 46 / 27. Context buckets: pre-2005 271,385 / 36,122 (13.31%, 16,340 distinct positive entities, SEQ_ACAO empty in this era); gap 2020-2021 excluded (18,419 / 4,861, 26.39%); 2026 excluded (10,562 rows, all censored). First-time vs repeat measured per year (2023: first-time 8,449 n / 1,524 pos = 18.0%; repeat 7,856 n / 3,878 pos = 49.4%); distinct entities overall 439,781 with autos-per-entity bins 1:335,785, 2:62,530, 3-5:32,272, 6-20:8,613, 21+:581. Base-rate drift across windows (17.8% -> 27.7% -> 28.4%) is a measured phenomenon property (era + enforcement regime). Clustering for the gate's enough_clustered_positives check: positives cluster by entity (serial infringers) and by fiscalizacao action (SEQ_ACAO_FISCALIZATORIA) - thousands of distinct clusters per window, so the camara-style year-cluster failure cannot occur; entity (or entity+action) is the natural event key.
records.target: Binary label: exists another auto de infracao in the same published table with identical CPF_CNPJ_INFRATOR and DAT_HORA_AUTO_INFRACAO in (T, T+365 days], where T is the current auto's lavratura instant. Label source columns: CPF_CNPJ_INFRATOR and DAT_HORA_AUTO_INFRACAO; both excludable from shipped features (entity keys shipped hashed). Censoring: right-censoring at the last observed lavratura date in the extract; entities leaving enforcement attention are treated as no re-autuacao observed (this is a re-AUTUACAO task, not a reoffense task - enforcement effort confound stated in the task card, not hidden). MEASURED 2026-11-04: label computed on raw CPF_CNPJ_INFRATOR equality - entities are stored in canonical punctuated form (672,780/672,793 non-empty rows carry ./- punctuation; digit-normalized length is 11 for 453,978 cpf rows (64.4%) and 14 for 218,797 cnpj rows (31.0%); 32,874 missing (4.7%, concentrated pre-1995), 18 other) - so construction MUST normalize to bare digits before joining and hashing; the probe's raw-equality rates are the measured baseline. Publisher cross-check of the entity classification: TP_PESSOA_INFRATOR matches the digit-based split exactly (2023: PF 9,929 = cpf11 9,929; PJ 6,376 = cnpj14 6,376). Right-censoring measured at the extract's max lavratura 2026-10-30: 2,347 rows of 2025 and all 10,562 rows of 2026 fall inside the unobserved 365-day window. Status-mix design input: 2023 carries Lavrado 16,250 (99.0%), Cancelado 146, Excluido 10, Substituido por outro 3; SIT_CANCELADO='S' is ~1%/yr - construction must state which side of the population these rows fall on.

records.prediction_time: Prediction instant = the official publication date of the sitting's individual results (dated example, Colombia Time COT=UTC-05:00, no DST): sitting T = Calendario A school-year 2025, exam applied Sunday 2025-08-10 (ICFES calendar PDF 2025_Calendario11A_V03.pdf; ICFES news 2025-08-08 '640 mil personas presentaran las pruebas Saber 11 calendario A' este domingo 10 de agosto; some municipalities reprogrammed to 2025-08-31 per news 2025-08-12), individual results published Friday 2025-10-10 (calendar PDF row 'Publicacion de resultados individuales Saber 11 en pagina web: viernes 10 de octubre de 2025'). INSTANT = 2025-10-10 COT (hour not stated by the publisher; date-level instant). Feature event window closes at the instant: school aggregates for sittings <= T are published (with sitting T's results, ICFES also publishes its per-school aggregate reports - 'Otros resultados examen Saber 11': Clasificacion de Planteles, Reportes de Resultados Agregados). Eligibility at instant: school has >=10 scored examinees with valid PUNT_GLOBAL in sitting T (measured school counts per sitting: 10,701-12,778 at n>=10 of 11,906-13,748 raw). Target window = Calendario A school-year T+1 sitting: exam applied ~August T+1 (2026 Cal-A sitting: results-publication news dated 2026-09-22), results published ~Sept/Oct T+1 - the whole target window (exam, scoring, publication) falls ~11-13 months AFTER the instant; no part of it precedes the instant. AS-OF / VINTAGE POLICY (recorded limitation, not resolved): the open MICRODATA for a sitting is published on datos.gov.co with a long lag (measured: per-year 2020 datasets uploaded 2021-03-15; unified table's 2022 sitting appears at rowsUpdatedAt 2023-08-23), so the constructed panel is a CURRENT-VINTAGE RETROSPECTIVE panel: an operational system at the historical instant would have used ICFES's same-day aggregate reports, not the open microdata; no point-in-time operational claim is made for the microdata channel, and microdata revisions between snapshots are not excluded (the 'Resultados unicos' table is itself a publisher curation; ESTU_ESTADOINVESTIGACION is a publication-consent status, measured values 'PUBLICAR' 1,065,436 / 'VALIDEZ OFICINA JURIDICA' 452 for 20224). Label-definition caveat (measured): national sitting-level mean shifts between adjacent sittings are large (school-mean deltas: +8.35 (2015->2016), -2.97 (2016->2017), -8.83/-9.54 on Calendario B pairs) because ICFES equates scores per sitting, so an absolute-points decline label partially reflects national equating drift; construction must either define the label relative to the sitting's school-mean distribution (percentile-rank drop, equating-invariant) or ship sitting-level national aggregates as history features and state the conflation explicitly.

records.question: For a Colombian Calendario A secondary school whose Saber 11 school-year T sitting results are published (individual results are published on a dated official calendar, e.g. sitting 2025: exam applied 2025-08-10, individual results published 2025-10-10), predict whether the school's mean global score (PUNT_GLOBAL, 0-500 scale, school-year T+1 sitting) falls below its school-year T mean by at least a fixed margin. Features are the school's own published history up to and including sitting T: per-subject school means and cohort sizes for sittings <= T, school registry attributes (calendar, naturaleza oficial/no oficial, genero, jornada, bilingue, area, DANE department/municipality codes), and cohort context shares from the publisher's own questionnaire fields (FAMI_*: estrato, parental education, household assets), all documented in the publisher's 51-column schema with descriptions.
records.review: Five contracts reconciled against recorded evidence. (1) REDISTRIBUTION: supported for the anonymous channel - CC BY-SA 4.0 (licenceId CC_40_BY_SA) on the publisher's own official datasets with ICFES attribution (class B; attribution + share-alike carried into LICENSE.md); UNRESOLVED for the registration-gated DataIcfes bytes that the missing school-years (2018, 2021) and fresh tail (2023, 2024) would come from - terms unread, no grant assumed. (2) TIMING: supported - the instant is the publisher's own dated results-publication calendar (worked dated example 2025-10-10 COT; target window ~11-13 months after the instant, no part precedes it), with the current-vintage retrospective posture recorded explicitly (open microdata lags the instant by months-to-a-year; an operational system would have used the same-day aggregate reports) and the equating year-shift caveat recorded for the label definition. (3) TARGET: supported - label from the next school-year's published sitting aggregate; source column excludable by shipping only sittings <= T; eligibility from information at the instant; school non-persistence (no T+1 sitting) is observed absence, excluded and to be quantified at construction. (4) SPLIT CAPACITY: UNRESOLVED - the decisive blocker: the anonymous channel yields only 4 Cal-A transitions (2018-2/2021-2 absent from every published open copy, measured; third-party guide independently states the same), which cannot fill three disjoint windows; the complete Cal-B fallback (7 transitions, 283-308 schools) is viable but ~20x smaller and population-narrow - an explicit redesign decision, not a silent one; the publisher's own renovated-platform inventory claims Saber 11 1996-2024, and one bounded registration+listing probe settles either the full 2014-2024 Cal-A panel (10-11 transitions) or the fallback/park decision. MEASURED BLOCKER on the anonymous channel: only 4 consecutive Cal-A transitions exist (2014->15, 2015->16, 2016->17, 2019->20; 2018-2/2021-2 absent from all published open data, nothing after the 2022 school-year) - a 1-transition holdout is not a defensible window, so the anonymous channel alone cannot fill three windows. records.target: Binary label per (school, transition T->T+1): 1 if the school's mean PUNT_GLOBAL over its scored examinees in the Calendario A school-year T+1 sitting is lower than its school-year T mean by at least the fixed margin (margin or a percentile-rank variant chosen at construction; both measured feasible). Label source columns: PUNT_GLOBAL of sitting T+1 (and the sitting T+1 rows generally) - excluded from shipped features by construction (features use sittings <= T only). Measured base rates (schools with n>=10 examinees on both sides, server-side aggregates): any decline 52.42% / 20.66% / 62.54% / 51.04%; decline >=5 points 31.98% / 9.87% / 42.23% / 33.55%; decline >=10 points 16.08% / 4.45% / 24.01% / 19.69% for the four available Cal-A transitions 2014->15, 2015->16, 2016->17, 2019->20. Censoring: a school with no sitting-T results is not eligible (excluded, not imputed); a school with no T+1 sitting (closed/merged/moved to another calendar) is observed absence of an outcome and is excluded from the scored panel - construction must record the non-random-exit rate as part of the definition (school persistence measured: 9,025-10,952 of ~11.9-13.7k schools appear in adjacent sittings).

measurements.threshold_hunt_2026_10_23_pass2: RESOLVED: official per-station flood thresholds (cotas) exist and are extractable. records.prediction_time: Instant: 13:00 UTC on day D+1. Features are everything published by then with event time <= D: the complete detection archive through day D (daily file for D observed complete at 09:05 BRT on D+1; detections stream near-real-time at 10-minute granularity during day D), calendar, state/biome. Optional covariates also available at the instant: observed fire-risk grid for day D (NetCDF published ~03:32 server time on D+1) and INPE's forecast risk grids for D+1..D+3 (published on day D). Excluded as post-instant: every detection row with event time > D, and any current-year statistic that only becomes final later. As-of policy: each detection row carries its event timestamp (data_pas / data_hora_gmt); the archive is treated as an append-mostly observation log; LIMITATION (recorded): INPE regenerates archive files (2003-2017 files regenerated 2025-09-08; 2024 file regenerated 2025-06-06) and no historical file vintages are kept, so features are taken from the current archive under the policy that detection rows are immutable observations; construction pins file checksums and must re-fetch one fixed month after >=2 weeks to measure late-row churn before quoting any number.

records.question: A Brazilian municipality has recorded zero active-fire detections (INPE reference-satellite series) for 14 consecutive days through day D. At 13:00 UTC on day D+1 - after INPE's morning consolidation of day-D detections (daily CSV for day D observed published 09:05 BRT on D+1) - given only the municipality's detection history through day D, the calendar, state and biome, will at least one active-fire detection be recorded in that municipality within the next 7 days (event days D+1..D+7)? A useful prediction lets PREVFOGO/IBAMA, state civil defence and municipal fire brigades pre-position crews in a country where detection precedes enforcement, and persistence cannot win by construction.

findings: Target window [D+1 00:00, D+8 00:00) begins 13 hours before the 13:00 UTC D+1 prediction instant; label information precedes prediction.

INPE FAQ Q39: Base 2 launched 14 Jun 2018, replaced Collection 5 with 6, reprocessed Terra history since 01 Nov 2000 and Aqua since 04 Jul 2002, corrected 2017 MODIS/VIIRS detections, moved to IBGE 2016 boundaries. Historical rows are retrospectively reprocessed, not operational snapshots.
Current regenerated files and a prospective two-week churn check do not establish historical as-of availability; Last-Modified is not completeness or time zone.
