records.split_strategy: Windows by fire year (July-June or calendar year - construction fixes one definition and records it), temporal, non-overlapping: train 2003-2019, eval 2020-2022, holdout 2023-2025, each window carrying full seasonal cycles. Every measured year holds both classes at large margin: municipality-days with >=1 detection 2019: 53,369; 2020: 54,956; 2022: 49,559; 2024: 62,450 (positives cluster in the dry season and in drought years - reported as clustered counts; onset-conditioned pairs measured on 2024: 1,173,526 evaluated pairs, 88,888 positives = 7.57% base rate; raw pairs 1,535,182 with 244,175 positives = 15.9%). Exact per-window pair counts are computed on the full files at construction (all 23 ref years measured feasible: 4 years = 35.5 MB in 16.9 s on the coordinator). Reference-satellite era consistency: the publisher curates the reference series for comparability and the Estatisticas product uses the same series (cross-check exact), but construction must record the per-era reference satellite from INPE documentation and pin window boundaries on any era change observed in the yearly counts.
records.target: Binary. Positive: >=1 reference-satellite detection with event timestamp in [D+1 00:00, D+8 00:00) located in municipality m; negative: zero such detections. Label source: the same detection rows (data_pas timestamp + municipio/estado name) that feed the feature history - construction derives the label from event-time windows and must not ship any row with event time > D in feature columns (the label column is a derived aggregate, never a carried source column). Population: all Brazilian municipalities (5570 IBGE codes; ref-era files key by name - construction maps names to IBGE codes and asserts the mapping is total over the detection rows). Conditioning: evaluated pairs are municipality-days with zero detections in [D-13, D] (onset-conditioned; raw-pair variant recorded for comparison).

records.split_strategy: Candidate partition (to be confirmed by the worker aggregate-count job before status ready): filing-application_date windows train 1995-2013 / eval 2014-2018 / holdout 2019-2023, with an eligibility cutoff excluding filings whose outcome window is not yet closed at the extract date (pending share per filing year is being measured to set the cutoff; recent filings 2024+ are expected to be censored-heavy). Positives cluster in calendar time (examination practice changes, filing booms), so the conservative independent-positive count is per filing year, reported beside the row count. Splits are computed from the source by the worker job; both classes must be present in every window. Confirmed measured by ipa-tm-002 2026-11-04: both classes present in every window, censoring <=0.76% through filing year 2023 (2024: 2.14%, 2025: 17.7%, 2026: 78.1%), positive rate drifts 68.6% (train) -> 74.9% (eval) -> 79.2% (holdout 2019-2023).
records.target: Label: whether the application ever achieves registration - a standing (is_standing=TRUE) registered event in the trade-mark events table, cross-checked against the application table's gained_registration_status_date and current status. Retroactively expunged registrations (is_standing=FALSE - revocation that legally 'unhappened' the grant, per the dictionary's 'What is is_standing?' section) do NOT count as registered. Post-registration lifecycle (ceased/removed/expired after grant, non-use removal) does not change a positive label. Negative: application terminated before any registration (refused/rejected/withdrawn/lapsed pre-registration/not_filed/cancelled/voided/linked). Censored: applications with no registration and no pre-grant terminal event at the extract date (recent filings, or rare very slow prosecutions) - excluded by eligibility cutoff, never silently dropped. Label source columns (events, status, registration dates) are excluded from shipped features.

The entire event universe under the November 2015 commitment baseline is 197 advisory records: 158 lifted + 39 currently in effect (the site narrative of 2026-09-10 counts 38 active in 36 communities; the export on 2026-10-20 lists 39). DateSet years span 1995-2025, so lift events are bounded by the ~11-year program window: about 14 lift events per year, all decided by one federal program's capital-project pipeline, clustered by region (ON 110/197 events, SK 30, MB 22, BC 20, ATL 8, AB 4, QC 3) and by federal funding waves; 39 advisories are right-censored still-active. The 158 lifted-advisory records carry AdvisoryID, AdvisoryType, CategoryID, CommunityName, CommunityNum, WaterSystemName, DateSet, DateLTDWASet, DateExpected (a projected lift date), CorrectiveMeasure, LongPhase, PopulatioEstimated, RecommendedEPHO/RecommendedEPHODate/RecommendedEPHOIND, Region, coordinates - and no DateLifted. records.question: At a consumer-product recall's first publication on the METI recall register (リコール日/掲載日, Asia/Tokyo), predict whether the register will later record a substantive lifecycle update on that recall - 対象追加 (affected-scope addition), 型番追加 (model addition), 品番追加・対象期間拡大 (item/period expansion) or 対策内容更新 (countermeasure change) - within a pre-registered window, using only information published at the first instant (product sub-category, product name, implementing business incl. domestic/overseas-importer marker, initial date, sales period, affected-unit count, hazard/remedy fields - per-field availability to be verified on the detail pages). records.prediction_time: Prediction instant: 00:00 JST on day t (equivalently the end of day t-1). Features: hourly pollen counts at the station and paired AMEDAS weather, all timestamps <= 23:59 JST day t-1; no same-day values. Historical real-time availability: while it ran, the system published hourly updates (MOE press 4673: '1時間ごとに更新', real-time web display), so an operational user at day t-1 23:59 had all feature values. VINTAGE CAVEAT (recorded, not resolved): the archive is a post-season cleaned vintage - the in-file code -9996 explicitly marks values removed after comparing '前後の時間や周辺観測値' (neighbouring hours/stations), i.e. post-hoc quality edits a real-time user would not have had; blank/-9997/-9998 mark comms outage/Asian dust/snow outages. The task therefore claims NO historical operational availability and is labelled retrospective; the as-of policy is 'archive vintage, as downloaded 2026-10-28'. Station-eligibility for scored rows must be computed from a trailing pre-instant window (e.g. valid days in the last 14 days before t), never from full-season validity, to avoid future-conditioned inclusion.

records.split_strategy: Retrospective station-day benchmark on the closed MOE Hanako archive (program terminated 2021-12-24; no operational-availability claim - see prediction_time vintage caveat). Panel: station x day for the Feb-June sugi seasons 2006-2021 (16 seasons, 90-135 station columns/season, 7,813-13,221 valid station-days per season). Label: station-day 24-hour total >= threshold (construction picks from the measured distribution; candidate thresholds 40/80/160/320/640/1280 grains/m3 all recorded). Candidate windows (temporal, disjoint): train 2006-2013 (8 seasons, 90,423 valid station-days, 77,957 positives at 80), eval 2014-2017 (4 seasons, 45,832 valid, 39,624 at 80), holdout 2018-2021 (4 seasons, 48,947 valid, 39,626 at 80). Clustered effective sample = seasons (16), since same-day station counts within a region move together; season-level cluster counts must be reported with scores. 2003-2005 seasons excluded (layout unparsed).
records.target: Binary: sum of the station's 24 hourly counts on day t (JST) >= threshold, with a censoring rule excluding day t from scored rows when fewer than 20 of 24 hourly values are valid (valid = non-missing per the in-file codes: blank = unobserved/comms outage, -9996 = other/unatural removed, -9997 = Asian-dust interference, -9998 = snow interference). Threshold OURS (construction decision): the archive publishes no daily category table for the automatic counters (the real-time site's 4-level colour scheme is not documented as numeric daily totals in the archive), so a base rate at a candidate threshold (e.g. a JWA-style daily-total level) is measured at construction, not asserted now. Units: grains/m3 (個/m3), volumetric KH-3000 counts; the MOE labels the real-time display 'スギ花粉数' ('for the time being, sugi pollen count') per press 4673 - whether the archive column is sugi-only or sugi+hinoki total is a documentation check at construction (single count column per station per file; no taxon split in the files). Label source column (day-t counts) is excludable from features by construction (features are strictly <= t-1).

The pattern now recorded twice in Kenya (CBK auction data, PPIP procurement data) is that Kenyan government data instruments default to bare 'All rights reserved' copyright even where an executive order mandates disclosure; future Kenya-focused sessions should read the footer FIRST and budget no more than a channel sweep before closing.

records.split_strategy: Temporal splits on ISO-week transitions, disjoint and ordered: candidate windows (to be fixed at construction from the full 58-month archive, ~250 weekly transitions 2022-01..2026-10): train on transitions up to 2024-12, eval on 2025 transitions, holdout on 2026 transitions (exact windows fixed at construction). Each weekly transition carries both classes: measured increase rate 15.5%-22.2% and decrease rate 14.5%-20.1% across all 7 measured transitions (Aug-Sep 2026, 10% premise subsample), so class balance holds window-to-window. Positives cluster by item: 54-58 distinct items show >=1 increasing pair per transition, and the top-10 items carry 38-45% of positive pairs - the clustered event count (item-level, not pair-level) must be reported per split and is ~55/week in the subsample (~170/week full panel, estimate). Cross-split identifier policy: item-premise pairs (and premises/items) recur across windows by design - the panel is longitudinal - so entity keys are NOT split-exclusive; the no-cross-split-entities check does not apply to pair panels where the same pair legitimately appears in many weekly transitions. This must be declared in quality.json (expected_duplicate_ids / documented repeats) at construction, mirroring the runner-contract handling of longitudinal panels.
records.target: Binary: modal(price of item i at premise p over all observations in ISO week W+1) > modal(same over week W). Modal price = most frequent observed price that week (ties broken by higher price, deterministic). Pairs with <3 observations in either week are excluded from that transition's rows (exclusion is a function of data through week W+1, applied identically everywhere; it affects ~3% of subsample pairs). The label source columns are the W+1 price observations themselves: no price observation with date > end of week W may ship as a feature column; the shipped target is 0/1.

records.target: Binary label per (origin, destination, day T): pair ridership on day T >= a fixed pair-specific reference threshold (construction selects: per-pair training-window percentile, e.g. p90, or a small set of absolute thresholds; candidate thresholds recorded from measured pair-year series in probe/pair_blocks_2024.json). Source column: 'ridership' (integer trips, publisher-documented as trips not necessarily passengers); it is the label source and is excludable from shipped features (shipped features are the SAME column's values at dates <= T-2 plus calendar - the label is its day-T value, which postdates the instant). Population: all ordered station pairs on the network with an active block in the source, excluding (a) rows with origin or destination 'A0: All Stations' (pseudo-station aggregate/censored rows, measured station-scale magnitudes ~4.4k/day, semantics to be verified against pair sums at construction), and (b) pairs whose destination is a Putrajaya Line station other than PYL03/PYL04 (32/34 PYL station codes never appear as destinations - confirmed by my own 2024-edition sampling AND by a public data-request thread id 216 dated 2026-10-24; censoring, not zero demand). records.question: At a day-ahead instant, predict whether the Nigerian national grid will record a total or partial system collapse on the following day, from published grid-operating history (generation, frequency, load). Closed at the licence gate before any task probing; the secondary task-shape and timing observations below are from the publisher's published report text, not from a constructed dataset.
records.review: The grid-collapse task is the most evocative Nigeria story this tick, and closing it took three cheap instruments to read, not three weeks of PDF scraping: footer, terms page, report front matter. The general lesson the record carries for Nigeria: NBS prohibited (class D), NERC silent-with-copyright (class C) - the two most task-shaped Nigerian publishers are both licence-blocked, so a Nigeria-focused session should budget for reading terms first and expect closures.

sources.name: NERC quarterly and annual reports (grid event tables and operational aggregates)

records.split_strategy: Not reached (licence veto). Scale planning on any reopen: ~90 recorded collapse events 2016-2025 (publisher's own figures quoted in target_definition), declining sharply after 2020; three disjoint windows with both classes present is plausible on the day-grain population but positives are strongly year-clustered; no counts were computed.
records.target: Binary (collapse day vs non-collapse day; optionally total vs partial). Label source: NERC's unit-level system-collapse event tables in quarterly and annual reports (date, time, type, immediate cause, restoration date/time; e.g. 2025 Annual Report Table 24 'System Collapses in 2019 - 2025'). Event-grain positives are sparse and declining: NERC order NERC/2023/035 (published figures) lists partial/total 2016: 6/22, 2017: 9/15, 2018: 1/12, 2019: 1/10, 2020: 0/4, 2021: 2/2, 2022: 2/4, 2023: 0/3; the 2024 Annual Report records 9 incidents in 2024; the 2025 Annual Report records 2; the 2026 Q1 report records 2 (one total 23 Jan, one partial 27 Jan). Roughly 90 events 2016-2025 against ~3,650 days, with positives clustered within crisis years. The deeper timing defect: daily-resolution features are NOT published in bulk - NERC's operational data products are monthly/quarterly aggregates (average daily system frequency by month, average hourly generation) plus the event tables themselves, so a day-ahead operational task cannot be assembled from published features without a feature source that has not been identified.

records.prediction_time: June 1 of year Y+1: the statutory deadline for year-Y NPRI reports (NPRI reports for a calendar year are due by June 1 of the following year, per the publisher's Canada Gazette NPRI notices and reporting guides). MEASURED 2026-11-03 (timezone-precise, from the publisher's own FAQ and Gazette notice, both read via web search excerpts): 'the reporting deadline is 11:59 p.m. Eastern Daylight Time (EDT) on June 1', extended to 11:59 pm EDT the following business day when June 1 falls on a weekend; the 2021-2023 Canada Gazette notice itself names the adjusted dates 'June 1, 2023, June 3, 2024 and June 2, 2025' (2024-06-01 was a Saturday, 2025-06-01 a Sunday - both verified). So the exact instants are 2023-06-01, 2024-06-03, 2025-06-02 23:59 America/Toronto. At that instant the facility's full history through year Y is knowable, and its year-Y+1 outcome is not - the Y+1 report would not even be due until June 1 (+weekend adjustment) of Y+2, and the publisher publishes each reporting year's data later still (the 2024 single-year file is the latest published as of 2026-10-19; 2025 reports are due 2026-06-01). FEATURES-ARE-FILER-KNOWN AT THE INSTANT: the open.canada.ca single-year package was re-created 2026-04-30 (a re-publication artifact like CRA's; portal dates do not evidence first publication), so at the deadline instant the year-Y reports are NOT yet third-party published - exactly the CRA pattern. ADVANCEMENT PICKS ONE HONEST FRAMING AS ITS FIRST STEP (the cqc precedent): (a) deadline instant (recorded here) - retrospective filer-information scope with the explicit assumption stated (za-cct precedent, no operational third-party availability claim); (b) year-Y-data publication instant - fully third-party operational at the cost of a later instant. Label semantics identical under both. Files are current-vintage (single-year package modified 2026-04-30; both files byte-size-stable between 2026-10-19 and 2026-11-03 measurements, sha256 pinned today); no historical-vintage claim is made.

records.split_strategy: Temporal by the outcome year Y+1 (label year): train Y+1 in 2005-2015, eval 2016-2019, holdout 2020-2023. 2024 exists (38,762,396 B; 7,738 facilities measured 2026-11-03, correcting the earlier '7,986+' note) but 2025 is not yet published, so 2024 exits are not observable; 2024 rows serve as feature history only. Measured base rates (full NPRI_ID set comparisons over complete single-year files): 2021->2022 exit 902/7,322 = 12.32%; 2022->2023 815/7,521 = 10.84%; 2023->2024 1,063/7,986 = 13.311% (measured 2026-11-03) - both classes amply present every year; ~800-1,063 positives per recent year means train (~11 label years) ~5-9k positives, eval ~3-4k, holdout ~3-4k (pre-2010 years have fewer facilities; counts to be recomputed from the bulk file at construction). Positives cluster by facility (a facility can exit at most once, but its history spans many year-rows) AND by province (AB 588 + SK 262 = 80% of 2023->2024 exits), so facility is the clustered unit and province/sector clustered counts are reported per window at construction: runner id = unique (NPRI_ID, Y) row key, NPRI_ID ships only as a declared high-cardinality column, never the id column.
records.target: Binary and mechanical, from the publisher's own per-year products: positive iff NPRI_ID is present in the year-Y single-year data file and absent from the year-Y+1 file. NPRI_ID is the publisher's permanent facility identifier (measured: facility NPRI ID 1 carries the same ID across 2021-2024 files). Absence means the facility reported no releases/disposals/transfers for that reporting year - the documented outcome of closure, falling below reporting thresholds, or ceasing to meet criteria; the task does not need to distinguish those causes because the label is the publisher's own reporting record, not a judgement. DNMC NUANCE (measured 2026-11-03 from the publisher's reporting guide): a facility that reported last year but no longer meets criteria 'is required to submit a Does Not Meet Criteria (DNMC) report' by the same deadline - construction must measure whether DNMC submissions appear in the published year files (e.g. zero-quantity rows) and state which side of the label they fall on; the mechanical presence/absence label is unaffected either way, but the limitation must be explicit.

Measured 2026-11-05 by probe/followup_2016_GLD_38.py (cow api/1/cow.json, wfo=GLD year 2016, phenomena=TO significance=W; evidence in probe/out/followup_2016_GLD_38.json; run log .factory/nws-tornado-build-001/container.log). So cow's (year, wfo, eventid) is NOT a unique warning key: each warning's own verify is correct for its own polygon/window; the pre-registered disagreeing-verify refusal fired on a false positive (distinct warnings, not one corrupted warning). Consequence for the rebuild: (a) the row key must become unique per warning (product_id, or (year,wfo,eventid)+product_id) and row_id must disambiguate them; (b) the dup_kept_earliest branch (agreeing verify, differing bytes -> keep one) can silently DROP a distinct warning - the same measured event is the test case, both warnings must survive as rows; (c) keep the byte-identical-dup drop and the disagreeing-verify refusal for genuinely same-product duplicates; (d) per-year row deltas in the failed run exceeded dup_identical for several years (2008 -6 vs 3; 2009 -10 vs 5; 2011 -51 vs 41; 2012 -33 vs 6), consistent with kept-earliest merges and/or unparsable-window skips - the rebuild's ledger must attribute every dropped row per year before relaunch; the raw-feature anchors (2013 1832/441, 2023 2531/656) are key-independent and unchanged. Cheapest discriminating next check (done): the single-WFO year pull above; next cheapest before rebuild is a local re-key of the cached anchor years 2013/2023 asserting the new key is unique and counting eventid collisions per year.

records.prediction_time: The warning's issue timestamp. Everything the warning product itself carries at issuance is a feature: issuing WFO, forecaster of record, issue/expiry times (hence time-of-day and day-of-season), the warned county list, the storm-based polygon geometry (area, perimeter, polygon-vs-county size reduction), the tornado-possible flag on parent SVR warnings, the hail/wind tags, and - via the per-warning product-text URL - the full issued text (tornado tag, damage-threat tag, storm motion). The label is determined afterwards by which tornado reports occur in the polygon while the warning is live; the cow fields that encode it (verify, stormreports, stormreports_all, lead0, areaverify, statuses, status) are label-source/post-hoc and never ship as features.

sources.name: IEM Cow API - NWS storm-based warning verification
IEM Cow documentation and verification methodology
NWS severe weather warning verification procedure (the official concept cow reimplements)

records.split_strategy: Temporal by issue year, all three windows contiguous and disjoint. Proposed: train 2008-2018 (storm-based polygons began Oct 2007), eval 2019-2021, holdout 2022-2024. Anchor measurements support capacity but window totals are computed at construction: measured 2013 = 1,832 warnings / 441 verified (24.1%) spread over 100 distinct days with >=1 verified warning; measured 2023 = 2,531 / 656 (25.9%) over 115 distinct days. Positives cluster by outbreak day, so the clustered count (100-115 independent positive days per measured year) is the figure that matters for window capacity, not the row count. Base-rate drift is a documented property of the source (warning POD peaked 2011, declined 2012-14, then recovered - WAF-D-23-0153), so multi-year windows and a drift note are required, not a single-year holdout.
records.target: Binary: the per-warning `verify` boolean returned by IEM cow for phenomena=TO, significance=W - whether >=1 tornado local storm report (buffered by cow's default 15 km) falls inside the polygon during the valid window. The method is documented on the cow page ('NWS Storm Based Warning Verification') and matches the official storm-based verification concept in NWS Instruction 10-1601 ('FAR is the number of false alarms (unverified warnings) divided by the total number of warnings'; storm report points verify warning areas).

records.prediction_time: The plan's public launch: the instant its requirements are first published (GHO publication in early December for the following plan year, or the plan's own release for late-launched plans). Dated example (all UTC): Afghanistan HRP 2023 (plan id 1117) - GHO 2023 launched 2022-12-01 with Afghanistan at $4.6B; the HRP itself launched end of December 2022 / early January 2023; prediction instant pinned at 2023-01-01T00:00Z. Every feature is fixed by that instant: original requirements (plan endpoint origRequirements = 4,627,363,573, matching the December 2022 GHO ask), plan type, country, and strictly-prior plan-years (all closed years, final values). The target window is the plan year 2023-01-01..2023-12-31, strictly after the instant. VINTAGE POLICY (the decisive timing finding): the HDX CSV 'requirements' column is CURRENT-vintage - of 836 plans with requirements, 286 were revised up and 166 down after launch, and the CSV shows the revised value in revised cases - so it must never be used as a launch feature; the plan endpoint's origRequirements is the launch-vintage denominator, verified against the December 2022 GHO on the Afghanistan fixture. Prior-year funding totals used as features are current-vintage final values for closed years, approximating what was knowable at launch (late-reported flows are the measured gap - flow records carry firstReportedDate and decisionDate; 94.5% decisionDate coverage in a 200-flow sample); this retrospective approximation is declared as the restricted protocol and probed at gate 1.5, not assumed to be operational forecasting.

records.question: For a UN-coordinated humanitarian appeal or response plan (HRP/CAP/flash appeal/HNRP/SRP and similar single-country plans) at its public launch instant (requirements first published - GHO early December for the following year, or the plan's own release, whichever the record dates), will the plan receive funding equal to at least 50% of its ORIGINAL (launch-vintage) requirements by the close of its plan year? Features are launch-time attributes (original requirements, plan type, GHO membership, country/region, emergency linkage) plus strictly-prior-year history for the same country (prior-year plan coverage, funding levels, series length). A useful prediction identifies, months ahead, which appeals will end the year underfunded - the quantity GHO gap analysis reports after the fact - enabling donor advocacy and fundraising prioritization.

records.split_strategy: Temporal, on the primary population (782 single-country plan-years with origRequirements>0, 2000-2025), measured from the source on 2026-10-29 at the >=50%-of-ORIGINAL-requirements threshold: train 2000-2016: 437 rows, pos 282 / neg 155 (64.5%), 78 distinct countries; eval 2017-2020: 139 rows, pos 81 / neg 58 (58.3%), 51 countries; holdout 2021-2025: 182 rows, pos 96 / neg 86 (52.7%), 43 countries. Both classes present in every window. 2026 live-edge rows (24) excluded until their year closes. CLUSTERED COUNT (the honest sample size): 83 distinct country series in the primary population, max 28 plan-years for one country; positives also cluster by year through global funding cycles - measured positive rate at the 50% threshold drifts 68.3% (2000-2013) -> 52.3% (2014-2018) -> 63.8% (2019-2022) -> 42.5% (2023-2025), and GHO coverage fell from ~50% (2022) to 38% (2023) per the publisher's own snapshot; intervals and baselines must be country-clustered and year-aware. The final window cut is construction's choice; these three windows are the measured default.
records.target: Binary: the plan's FTS funding total for its plan year (usage year = plan year; commitments + paid contributions, pledges excluded, USD, publisher's own attribution including boundary flows) divided by its ORIGINAL requirements (launch vintage) is >= 0.50 -> 1, else 0. Label source: per-plan-year funding totals (FTS flow endpoint incoming.fundingTotal with planId+year filter; equal to the publisher's HDX distribution on single-country rows - measured: Yemen HRP 2023 1,774,327,599, Afghanistan HRP 2023 1,678,347,238, both API==CSV to the dollar) and origRequirements from the plan endpoint; both excludable from features by construction (features carry launch attributes and strictly-prior years only). Censoring: plan-years whose year has not closed are excluded and counted (2026 live edge: 24 primary rows), never imputed. Zero-funding rows are the publisher's recorded outcome (empty funding fields in the HDX CSV counted at construction, not dropped silently). Population: PRIMARY = single-country plan-years with origRequirements > 0, 2000-2025 (782 rows; 60 multi-country regional plans excluded from the primary task because the HDX CSV splits them into country slices whose funding sum covers only ~78% of the plan total - measured on Burundi RRP 2021: slices 14,978,233 vs API plan total 19,282,778; regional plans can be a secondary population with flow-endpoint totals if construction wants them). Appeal-linked funding only; the country rows without plan linkage (2,678 HDX CSV rows, 'Not specified' plans) are outside the task population, so the label's meaning is single-population throughout.

records.question: The lead probed was the OECD GlobalRecalls portal (globalrecalls.oecd.org), the OECD Working Party on Consumer Product Safety's compilation of consumer product recalls contributed by ~47-50 national and regional authorities (launched 2012). The natural differentiated task was cross-jurisdiction propagation: at the portal publication of a product recall in jurisdiction A at instant T, will the same product be recalled in jurisdiction B within a fixed window? That is the one task shape this compilation could carry that no single national recalls portal can (in-house comparators hc-recalls-classification, openfda-food-recall-classification and rasff-notification-risk-decision are single-portal classification tasks on food/health products, not propagation). The session measured the source's coverage and closed the lead: the propagation target's negative class is censoring-dominated by heterogeneous contributor coverage, and the compilation adds no clean licence or unique access over the four reliably-contributing national portals.

records.question: At the filing instant of a specific instance - the day an interested party (individual, NGO, trade union, business or other submitter) submits a complaint to a National Contact Point (NCP) alleging that a multinational enterprise did not observe the OECD Guidelines - will the NCP accept the case for further examination at initial assessment (Step 3 of the procedure), or will the case be closed without proceeding ('not accepted', which per the publisher's own terminology also includes withdrawals before the initial assessment completes)? A useful prediction tells complainants whether and how a grievance framed this way is likely to clear the intake gate of the chosen NCP, tells companies and RBC observers which complaint profiles are likely to enter mediation, and gives the 52-NCP network a measurable intake-consistency signal across the functional-equivalence agenda the OECD itself tracks. Acceptance is a real institutional decision published 1-12+ months after filing (measured: 2021-2025 closed-cohort acceptance 54-63%), not an editorial artefact.
records.review: All five discovery contracts reconciled against recorded evidence (2026-11-03, discovery-only session; no construction, no worker). (1) Redistribution SUPPORTED - class A: OECD T&C grant Data use 'for any purpose, even for commercial use' absent additional restrictions, none found on the database or case pages; 2025 annual report is explicitly CC BY 4.0; attribution format prescribed ('[OECD (year), Title, URL]') and carried into LICENSE.md; the restricted-marked annual-report data annexes are excluded from any redistributed artifact. (2) Prediction timing SUPPORTED with one recorded assumption - instant = submission date (day grain, publisher-recorded per case), label event strictly after (initial assessment published 1-12+ months later; measured kr0029: filed 2026-02-27, decided 2026-05-21); the DB-coded complaint attributes (NCP, issue country, submitter class, sector, topics cited) are complaint-stated, but the codification itself is NCP/OECD-assigned in the current vintage - an ASSUMPTION to verify at construction on a bounded sample (compare DB topic codes against the complaint text in the linked initial-assessment statements; a material mismatch downgrades those columns to post-hoc and they are dropped); DB listing dates measured as unusable for timing (0 to ~32-month lag); current-vintage posture explicit (DB migrated platform June 2025, no historical vintages; inclusion timing discretionary per the publisher's FAQ - quoted). (3) Target SUPPORTED - binary acceptance at initial assessment derived from the publisher's own Status taxonomy (quoted Box-terminology: closed = concluded OR not accepted, incl. pre-assessment withdrawals; in progress = pending); label source column excludable (Status/Outcomes/Procedural issues/summaries never shipped as features); censoring handled by eligibility (terminal status at extraction), not by treating pending as negative. (5) Not a mirror SUPPORTED as differentiated - the OECD publishes the registry and aggregate reports but no prediction task; the nearest prior art is an academic hand-coded dataset of 81 human-rights cases concluded 2012-2021 scored on remedy gravity (Springer chapter, descriptive, not distributed in ML-ready form, different population and different target), named in the novelty check; no ML-ready NCP acceptance/conclusion benchmark found in catalog or literature searches. RISKS named for the construction gate: (a) the WB-instrument-family defect - if a trailing NCP(+submitter-class) rate table matches the model, there is no headroom and the candidate drops at baseline (the reference triad is therefore mandatory: global prior, NCP trailing rate, NCP x submitter-class trailing rate); (b) topic-codification timing (assumption above); (c) small-population clustering (top-5 NCPs = 52% of recent filings; ~120-190 rows per window) - the honest effective-sample and cluster counts must accompany any quoted score.

records.split_strategy: PROPOSED windows by submission year, disjoint; exact per-window row and label counts are the FIRST construction measurement (they require the full 700-case scrape - bulk work, worker), so the numbers below are the publisher's own reported aggregates plus measured closed-cohort acceptance rates, never presented as full-DB counts. Unit = one specific instance (DB case ID). Train: filings 2000-2017 (publisher filings table 2011-2017 sums to 217; pre-2011 filings approximately 203 from DB total 700 minus 2011-2025 - approximate, to be measured exactly at construction). Eval: filings 2018-2021 (189 per the publisher's table; all resolved by extraction - measured 2021 cohort: 63% accepted/37% not accepted). Holdout: filings 2022-2024 (152 per the publisher's table, minus rows still 'In progress' at extraction; measured cohort acceptance 2024: 58%, 2025: 54%). 2025-2026 filings are EXCLUDED from scored rows: the 2025 cohort is mostly still pending (publisher's data annex: at end-2025, of the 120 received in 2025, 99 in progress, 19 not accepted, 2 concluded; restricted-marked annex cited as cross-check only - construction re-measures censoring exactly from the DB). Both classes measured in every recent closed cohort (2021: 27/16, 2024: 30/22, 2025: 30/26). Cluster structure to measure at construction: cases cluster by lead NCP (top-5 NCPs hold 52% of 2025 submissions), by respondent company (repeat filings against the same company occur, incl. coordinated multi-NCP campaigns), and by submission year (the 2025 individual-submission surge is a cohort effect: 71% of 2025 submissions vs 23% in 2024) - the clustered count and an interval on it are required outputs of the first construction measurement, per the discovery policy.
records.target: Binary label per specific instance: 1 = the NCP accepted the case for further examination at initial assessment (DB Status values indicating acceptance: 'Concluded' after acceptance, or an in-progress-but-accepted state; the publisher's status taxonomy from the case records and the annual reports: closed = concluded OR not accepted, in progress = awaiting initial assessment OR accepted and ongoing); 0 = the case did not proceed past initial assessment ('Not accepted', which the publisher defines to include cases withdrawn prior to completion of the initial assessment). Source columns: the DB case-record 'Status' field (label source; excludable - not shipped as a feature) with 'Outcomes', 'Procedural issues' and all prose summaries excluded from features as post-hoc. Rows with Status 'In progress' at extraction are excluded from scored splits (censored, not negative). Label derivation needs no external data and no threshold.

measurements.mirror_texture_2026_10_22: The catalogue is a secondary aggregator for task purposes: the FUA/Cities family and national-accounts family republish indicators whose primary publishers are national statistical offices (the OECD's own metadata attributes series to national sources), the inventory itself carries non-OECD agency flows (ESTAT, IAEG-SDGs), and the World Bank WDI / Eurostat / FRED ecosystem republishes overlapping OECD series - a task built here would compete with the same numbers from many channels. The OECD's one row-level public product family, the global recalls portal (recalls.oecd.org), aggregates member-state recall datasets - the bench already holds the Health Canada recalls candidate (hc-recalls-classification) and US recall tasks, so that would be a mirror of work already represented.

records.split_strategy: Temporal by decision year, counts computed from the source (probe_count.py, 2026-10-31 files, s78_core = Planning Appeal + Householder (HAS)): train 2016-2020 (older file) 65,483 rows, 19,577 allowed (29.9%); eval 2021-2022 (complementary halves of 2021 from both files: 10,199+3,442) 27,179 rows, 8,044 allowed (29.6%); holdout 2023-2026 (5-yr file, 2026 through October) 52,471 rows, 16,273 allowed (31.0%). Both classes present in every one of the 11 decision years (yearly allow rate 27.0%-34.6%, no drift). Positives are independent appeal events; the main clustering is by LPA (376-379 distinct) and by linked cases (Link Status/Lead Case present, 0 duplicate case numbers within each file) - an LPA-clustered bootstrap interval is planned for the reference comparison. Cross-file dedup must key on the composite (Type of Casework, LPA Name, Received/Valid/Decision dates, Decision) because the Older Casework Data reference numbers are explicitly NOT linkable to Casework Database case numbers (publisher-documented).
records.target: Binary from the publisher's Decision field (documented data quality 'Good'): positive = 'Allowed', negative = 'Dismissed'. Pre-specified eligibility rule: labelled population = s78_core casework types with Decision in {Allowed, Dismissed}; 'Split Decision' (1,350 5-yr / 1,440 older, all types) and 'Allowed in part' rows are excluded from the core task rather than coerced (recorded masses; a variant may map split->positive). Excluded outcomes (measured, all types): Unknown 3,186+1,969, No Decision Code Associated 148+72, Invalid 237+136, Turned Away 9+11, Appeal Withdrawn 243+169, missing 178+600. Enforcement/RoW/TPO/high-hedges casework uses a different outcome vocabulary (Notice upheld / varied and upheld / quashed) and is out of scope. Censoring is stated: the database contains DECIDED cases only (publisher: in-progress, withdrawn and turned-away cases are not included), so the population is outcome-conditioned by construction; the task is 'among validated appeals that reach a PINS decision, which succeed', not 'among all validated appeals'. Decision and Decision Date columns are excluded from shipped features.

Urban Planning 'Transforming urban planning through machine learning' - classifies Australian planning applications into development categories from description text (DeBERTa-v3 F1 0.944); text classification, not decision prediction; data available 'on reasonable request', not published ML-ready. measurements.status_vocabulary_2026_11_06: Extracted from the register's own bundle public-register.min.js (PRstatusObj, verbatim descriptions): Lodged 'The application has been formally lodged by the applicant and is ready for assessment.'; Under Assessment '...awaiting decision.'; Approved 'The is approved.'; Decision Made 'Assessment of this application has completed and a decision has been made.'; Granted 'The is granted.'; Decision Under Appeal 'The decision made on the application by the relevant authority is being appealed in court, and may be upheld or overturned.'; Cancelled 'The was cancelled.'; Withdrawn 'The applicant has withdrawn this application from assessment and no decision may be made.'; Refused 'This was refused.'; Rejected 'This was rejected.'; Lapsed 'The decision made on this application has lapsed and is no longer valid.' measurements.statutory_timeframes_2026_11_07: Pathway timeframes read 2026-11-07 from the publisher's own guidance (plan.sa.gov.au 'Stages and timeframes' + 'Guide to Development Assessment' PDI PDF, via web search snippets): planning consent deemed-to-satisfy 5 business days; performance-assessed 20 (no notification/referral) / 50 (referral, assessment manager) / 70 (public notification, panel or SCAP authority); restricted 95; building consent class 1/10 20 (+10 if SCAP referral); land division 60; all plus 5 business days verification and 2 business days to issue; performance-assessed clocks can be SUSPENDED for information requests (up to 12 weeks, clock restarts) - a per-application latency label must carry this as a declared limitation since suspensions are not published per application. Full regulation-text extraction (PDI (General) Regulations 2017) and a published-late-decision known-event fixture remain open items for construction design.
measurements.worked_example_2026_11_06: Dated example (all dates Australia/Adelaide, ACDT UTC+10:30; register displays dates only, so instants are day-granular): application 26037018, 192 The Parade Norwood SA 5067. Feature event window: everything up to lodgement on 05/11/2026 - description 'Commercial' (internal fitout), applicant Jones Lang LaSalle, Assessment Pathway 'Accepted', elements 'Internal fitout', council 'Norwood Payneham and St Peters'. First availability: present in the register search results when fetched 06/11/2026 ~03:55Z, i.e. within one day of lodgement (publication latency bounded at ~1 day by this one observation, not proven generally). Eligibility cutoff: lodged via the portal on/after 31/07/2020 (PDI Act); DEV-Act rows exist for some authorities. Prediction instant: lodgement, 05/11/2026 (ACDT). Target start/end: the decision event; observed status 'DECISION MADE' with 'Development Approval - Planning, Building - Granted' by fetch time 06/11/2026 ~04:15Z, so this application's decision window closed within ~1 day of lodgement (Accepted pathway; not representative of notified/assessed pathways). For a forward framing the whole target window follows the prediction instant; for this retrospective example the decision had already occurred at fetch time.

records.prediction_time: At lodgement of the application. Features displayed by the register that are documented at that instant: description (free text, e.g. 'Commercial', 'Verandah', 'Outbuilding (domestic storage shed)'), Assessment Pathway (e.g. 'Accepted'), Elements (e.g. 'Internal fitout', Demolition/Land division/Telecom codes DM/LD/TF/TA/RDT), Council area, Decision authority type (Assessment Manager / Assessment Panel / Council / DAC / Governor / Independent Assessor / Minister / SCAP / State Planning Commission), Act (DEV/PDI), applicant name, property address and title. Post-lodgement fields to exclude from features: status, decision, decision date, notification outcome, and any post-hoc reclassification. Two timing questions remain unresolved: (1) whether the displayed Assessment Pathway/category is exactly the value assigned at lodgement or a later-revised value (needs the PDI Act guidance pages); (2) no decision DATE has yet been observed on a detail page (only the decision TYPE on the Assessment tab), which blocks candidate A's latency label. The register is a current-state service: it showed applications lodged 05/11/2026 by the 06/11/2026 ~03:55Z fetch, and historical vintages are not archived, so a task built from it is retrospective with an explicit as-of assumption; decisions may also change after the fact (status vocabulary contains 'Decision Under Appeal', 'Lapsed').

records.target: FIXED family 2026-11-07; prevalence unmeasured. Primary label, binary: statutory-timeframe latency = decision date (DecisionDetails DD, e.g. '30 Apr 2021') minus lodged date exceeds the PDI Act assessment timeframe for the application's pathway. Pathway timeframes documented from the publisher's own 'Stages and timeframes' page (read 2026-11-07): deemed-to-satisfy 5 business days; performance-assessed 20 (no notification/referral), 50 (referral, assessment manager), 70 (public notification, panel/SCAP); restricted 95; building consent class 1/10 20 (+10 SCAP referral); land division 60; plus 5 business days verification up front and 2 business days to issue; AND a documented clock-SUSPENSION confounder (info requests, up to 12 weeks, clock restarts) that the register does not publish per application - the latency label must declare this as a limitation, and a published late decision is still needed as the known-event fixture. Secondary label, binary: refusal = per-consent DecisionDetails DRT in {Refused, Rejected} for the planning consent; 0 = granted/approved; Withdrawn/Lapsed/Cancelled and still-Under-Assessment rows are censored, not negatives (coarse statuses are backend-enforced: Status=Refused/Granted search POSTs return no rows while Status='Decision Made' returns 260,311 + rows, negative validated by positive control, notes s6.5). Population: PDI-era applications (lodged >= 31 Jul 2020) in the statewide register; the register also carries 73,464 DEV-act-era rows (measured, incl. 36,067 decided 2010-2019 and 26,532 decided 2000-2009) which are a different, state-referred population and are EXCLUDED from the frame. measurements.extraction_cost_measured: Per gazette: 355-576 KB, live fetch 0.1-2.0 s (four editions measured). Corpus estimate: 8 areas x ~52 editions/year x retrievable years (~6-7) = roughly 2,500-2,900 PDFs, ~1.0-1.5 GB - a worker job, never the coordinator; pypdf text extraction of one 32-page edition takes seconds locally.
measurements.gazette_structure_2026_11_05: Every A&D edition has the same 9-section layout (contents page measured): 1.1 new applications / 1.2 variation applications / 2.1 new granted / 2.2 new refused / 2.3 variation granted / 2.4 variation refused / 3 Schedule 4 / 4.1 withdrawn / 4.2 grants not taken up / 5.1 notices of public inquiries to be held / 5.2 decisions taken at public inquiries / 5.3-5.4 transport manager inquiries / 6 operating centre reviews / 7.1 licences surrendered / 7.2 licences terminated / 8 licences revoked without public inquiry / 9 corrections. Each entry is prefaced by its reference number (e.g. OF2094843 SI ALEX ACOZMEI LTD, directors, registered address, operating centre + postcode, authorisation counts, transport manager where applicable).
hazards: Refusal grounds (e.g. financial standing) are NOT in the listing - good for ex-ante validity, but if most refusals are driven by grounds invisible at T the achievable ceiling may be low; the refusal-grounds distribution is measurable from decision documents at construction and must be reported with any score.

Section volume drift across eras: 2021 and 2026 editions parse identically, but 2013-2016 era layouts (and the pre-2016 page format that carried no PDF attachments) are unverified; the coverage ledger decides the usable window.
Weekly refusal counts swing (0 in the 2021 sample week, 4 in the 2026 sample week): per-window class counts need the aggregate, not extrapolation from two editions.
Withdrawal semantics: 4.1 withdrawals are applicant choices, not regulator decisions; the binary label choice (refused-only vs refused-or-withdrawn) is a pre-registered construction decision.

Repeat applicants and multi-licence operators (e.g. GT Transport Services with three licence numbers in one decision) create entity clustering; cluster-aware splits/bootstrap by applicant name-key are required.
PI notices mix application inquiries (S13/S14) with enforcement (S26): the application-outcome population must filter by ground code, measured present in the notice text.

The gazette is a statutory public notice containing named individuals (directors, transport managers, drivers); construction should decide pseudonymisation of person names before any release (operator/centre fields are business data, cqc precedent for provider data).

Conceptually attractive - infrastructure-delivery stall prediction is a genuinely useful task genre absent from the bench - but this session could not establish the three contracts that matter: machine-readable access (host blocks our egress), label construction (few vintages, unstable base composition, unknown per-work history fields), and licence (terms unread). The lead is parked with exact reopening conditions rather than dropped: the access failure is environment-specific, and TCU's press archive documents the panel's scale and vintage cadence well enough to re-attempt cheaply once access exists. Prior art note: target-level ML on Brazilian public-works stall risk already exists as a dissertation on FNDE/Proinfancia data (94.79% acc, no public benchmark); a TCU-panel task would need a stated formulation contribution.

records.split_strategy: UNBUILDABLE FROM WHAT WAS REACHABLE: TCU documents a handful of vintages (2018, 2020, 2022, updates to April 2025). Per-work dated status history inside the panel (if it exists, e.g. a paralizacao date field) could rescue a single-vintage design, but that could not be verified: the panel app is unreachable from this egress. No split counts are claimed.

measurements.baserate_prefix_samples_2026_10_27: CAN CSV year-file prefixes (first ~256 KiB compressed, ordered by notice ID = early-January notices; explicitly NOT year-representative): 2019: 3,343 rows / 706 notices, NUMBER_OFFERS populated 64.4%, single-bid 704 (32.7% of populated), multi 1,450, zero 0, INFO_ON_NON_AWARD set 9.5%; 2021: 4,049 rows / 568 notices, populated 58.2%, single 749 (31.8%); 2023: 2,361 rows / 722 notices, populated 72.3%, single 731 (42.8%). measurements.link_verification_2026_10_27: FUTURE_CAN_ID populated in 10/10 complete rows of the CN 2019 prefix (all ESTIMATED=0) and in the first CN 2023 rows. measurements.novelty_prior_art_2026_10_27: The exact task exists in reproducible form: Acikalin, Gorgun, Kutlu & Tas, 'How you describe procurement calls matters: Predicting outcome of public procurement using call descriptions', Natural Language Engineering 30(6) 2024 (online 2023-08-10): four prediction tasks on THIS TED CSV subset (number of offers PNumOffers; single offer PSingleOffer; foreign-firm award; price overrun vs estimate), 333,832 notices, 80/20 train/test, scored transformers, and released code: github.com/utkuumur/HowYouDescribeProcurementCallsMatters. Adjacent prior art: Demiray, Ozbayoglu & Tas 2015 (bidder counts on TED); Gallego, Rivero & Martinez 2021; 'Intensifying Competition in Public Procurement' (Springer GIQ 2023, TED 2017-2020 offers modelling); ECA Special Report 28/2023 single-bidding dashboard (DG GROW TED CSV + DigiWhist opentender); MDPI Algorithms 2025 (SME winner + main activity, TED 2015-2023); Spanish bidder-recommender (Wiley 2020). ML-ready data compilations already public: PleIAs/TEDEUTenders (HF parquet by year), EUROPROCURE-10 (HF, 2016-2025), zalizedata TED+OCDS (HF/Kaggle, 6.3M notices - NC licensed, unusable for us, but demonstrates availability).

records.prediction_time: The TED publication instant of the contract notice (CN). The CN CSV export carries the buyer's dispatch date (DT_DISPATCH) and year; the exact publication date (PD) per notice is served by the anonymous TED Search API v3. Worked example in notes.md: CN 10-2023 dispatched 2022-12-28, published 2023-01-02+01:00 (Europe/Brussels); its linked award notice 371295-2023 was published 2023-06-21+02:00, i.e. the whole target window (award decision, offers received) follows the prediction instant.

records.question: At the TED publication of a contract notice (call for competition), will the linked award notice report that the procedure's lot received exactly one offer (single bid)?
records.review: The licence is clean (class B: Commission Decision 2011/833/EU reuse, attribution, no distortion, personal-data caveat handled by excluding contact-person fields), the access is unusually good for this bench (official annual CSV extracts plus an anonymous search API), and the official CN->CAN link column (FUTURE_CAN_ID) removes the main construction risk - which is precisely why the source is heavily mined. Both timing and target contracts are satisfiable, so this is not a weak-source rejection; it is a strong source whose obvious task is taken. Recorded so no future tick re-probes TED blind, and so the measured access map (CSV subset ends 2023; FT vocabulary split legacy/eForms; link fixtures) is reusable for any genuinely different formulation.

records.prediction_time: The instant the occurrence begins (OccDate/OccTime, with the documented local time zone via TimeZoneID). Everything the TSB records during or after the occurrence is excluded from the shipped features: TSB's accident/incident type assignment (its taxonomy embeds outcomes, e.g. 'NON-MAIN-TRACK TRAIN DERAILMENT (NO DAMAGE)'), all injury/DG-release/fire/evacuation/damage flags and counts, weather observations taken at the occurrence, track and rolling-stock attributes measured during the occurrence, investigation/deployment/closeout fields, process dates (ENTRY_DT, RELEASE_DT, DAILY_RELEASED_DT, OccClosedDate), the free-text Summary, and even ReportedDate/ReportedTime (the notification instant, which post-dates the onset) - the last is shipped only in the record's provenance, never as a feature. The casualty outcome unfolds after onset and is the label.

records.question: A railway occurrence begins at a known place, time and operating context on the Canadian network (crossing accident, derailment, trespasser event, fire, collision, movement exceeding limits of authority, ...). At that instant, given only pre-occurrence context - where (subdivision, nearest location, province, region, lat/long), which railway, when (date, time of day, season), and what the train was doing (activity type) - will the occurrence result in at least one casualty (fatality or any injury)?

DGPA HTTPS fails strict SSL validation (chain missing Subject Key Identifier), so probes used an unverified context; the browser accepts the chain.
measurements.effective_date_semantics_2026_10_31: Archive records are keyed by ANNOUNCEMENT date (title = NNN年M月D日...情形), and rows reference one effective day via phrase: '今天' rows -> effective = title date; '明天' rows -> effective = title date + 1. Sampled 10 records across 2001-2026: 9/10 are entirely 今天-phrased; one (2024-07-27, Gaemi) mixes 16 今天 + 10 明天 rows; one further 2025 record (114年11月11日) is 明天-phrased. Most records therefore carry the same-day (final) status for the title date; a minority (observed 2024+) are previous-evening announcements for the next day. CONSTRUCTION RULE: map each row's effective date from its 今天/明天 phrase, never from the title alone. The census's per-year counts attribute positives by title date, so a minority of 2024+ records shifts by +1 day; this does not change any split-capacity conclusion.
measurements.modern_label_extraction_2026_10_31: DGPA archive attachments carry machine-parseable per-county status rows across the whole span. The 2026-10-22 'shell only' reading for 2023-06-01/2025-09-30/2026-09-02 was a probe artifact: pid=13097 (2026-09-02) carries '屏東縣|春日鄉士文村:今天停止上班、停止上課。' - a township-level closure the old probe's county/phrase list missed. Worker census east-asia-measure-002 (exit 0, 280.2 s; 976 DGPA detail/attachment requests + 50 list pages): 500/500 announcements processed, 0 fetch errors; 476/500 records carry county rows, 24 records (all in 2013) have no attachment and no county rows anywhere (label absent - measured coverage gap); 216/500 records have >=1 county-wide full-day closure; 1,333 county-day full-closure positives total (measured: sum of per-year countyday_full in the report); 100 event runs (consecutive-date clusters) with full closures, run sizes 19,10,9,5,4,3...; per-year positives 2001-2026: every year has both classes (min 2 county-day positives in 2020, max 158 in 2024). Modern canonical phrases: '今天已達停止上班及上課標準' (closed) / '今天未達停止上班及上課標準' (open); old era uses 照常辦公/停止辦公 variants; district-qualified rows (township/school closures) appear from 2011 and must be excluded from the county-wide label. LIMITATION recorded for construction: rows share origins across windows, so a later entrant's origin-level aggregate can contain components of an earlier entrant's outcome years - partial information, not the parent's exact-copy exposure; the gate 1.5.0 cross-row probe must run on the built artifact with the aggregate features declared. records.question: At the instant the World Bank Board approves an IBRD loan (board_approval_date, a documented column: 'The date the World Bank approves the loan'), will that loan disburse at least 90% of its original principal amount over its life? (Alternative near-balanced threshold >=99% is measured and recorded; construction picks one and documents it.) A useful prediction enables disbursement-risk scoring at commitment time for portfolio management, borrower-side planning and development-finance research: roughly a third of IBRD lending historically fails to move 90% of its commitment, and that gap is the operational quantity WB cash planning and aid-delivery studies care about.
records.review: All five discovery contracts have measured evidence. (1) Redistribution: CC BY 4.0 stated on the dataset page and metadata API - class A. (2) Prediction timing: instant is the documented board_approval_date; all shipped features are static approval-time attributes, with one disclosed current-vintage caveat (region, flagged in the publisher's own column description) that construction must either drop or carry as a limitation; the whole label window follows the instant; censoring is measured and the population cutoff at 2017 approvals is explicit. (3) Target: ratio of two in-row columns, label sources excludable, zero-ratio instruments are genuine negatives (cancelled_amount documents them), not missing data. (4) Split capacity: both classes in all three windows with hundreds of independent country-year clusters; clustering by project_id and country-year is measured and the split rule accounts for it. (5) Not a mirror: no ML-ready disbursement-completion benchmark exists; prior art targets IEG ratings (different target, different table, already measured as no-headroom by our own dropped wb-ieg candidate). Headroom is the known open risk of this source family (the IEG task failed it) - that is a construction/qualification measurement, and the near-balanced >=99% variant plus the approval-time-only feature contract are the mitigations; the honest posture is to build and let the measured baselines decide, not to claim headroom now.

records.review: All five discovery contracts reconciled against recorded evidence (2026-11-06, discovery-only session; no construction, no score). (1) Redistribution SUPPORTED - class A: CC BY 4.0 dataset-level licence on both data.wto.org dispute packages (CKAN license_id measured via the API) plus the 'unrestricted official WTO documents and legal texts are free for public use' grant; caveats (BETA portal, non-commercial clause for publications, no-logo) recorded in measurements.licence_note_2026_11_06. (2) Prediction timing SUPPORTED - the instant is the circulation date of the DS-numbered request for consultations; every feature is documented by the publisher on the case page and in the request itself (agreements cited at filing); all later stage dates are outcome-side and excludable. Vintage: current-snapshot archive with a MEASURED coverage hole (the dates file ends DS543/2018; case pages carry 2019-2025) - the task is declared retrospective research with a current-vintage assumption (cpcb/afdb precedent); no operational as-of claim is made. (3) Target SUPPORTED - DSB panel establishment is the publisher's own procedural milestone, fully recorded per DS; censoring handled by a measured 24-month eligibility cutoff (97.1% resolution); 'no panel' is documented to mean not-established-by-cutoff, not settled (settlement notification is mostly absent - measured). (4) Split capacity SUPPORTED, measured from the publisher's own artifact: train 383/169, eval 100/67, holdout 55/37, both classes in every window, distinct positive pairs 89/48/28 (>20 minimum), plus a measured modern-tail extension option. (5) Not-a-mirror SUPPORTED - no ML-ready, split, scored task exists: prior art is econometric/game-theoretic escalation studies (Bernauer et al. 506-dyad selection models; KU Leuven SBI panel-phase model; Maggi & Staiger) and the Horn & Mavroidis legal-coding research dataset (507 disputes to 2016, 1,272 variables, 'only to be used for research purposes, and not for commercial purposes', World Bank/EUI mirrors) - a stale, research-terms coding dataset, not a benchmark; novelty verdict recorded via scripts/check-novelty.py. KNOWN RISK carried into construction: the label may be identity-dominated (complainant-respondent pair + era), the afdb/wb-loan family defect; the pre-registered triad must therefore include trailing pair/pair-year escalation rates and era priors as references to beat, with pair-clustered bootstrap intervals, and the deciding rule follows the standing order (headroom only if the model beats EVERY reference with a CI excluding zero; reference dominance -> drop).

licence_summary.status: No standard SPDX licence is declared; the operative instruments are the City of Cape Town Open Data Terms of Use (disclaimer-only: as-is, no warranty, no liability; no restriction on reuse, redistribution or derivatives for portal data) together with the Council-approved Open Data Policy 27781 ('freely used, shared and built-on by anyone, anywhere, for any purpose'), and the ArcGIS item's licenseInfo links the portal terms. records.target: Binary: evening-peak exceedance. Label = (max half-hourly MVA over 16:00-22:00 SAST on day D for substation S) > (95th percentile of the same substation's evening peaks over the trailing 90 evenings ending strictly before the instant, minimum 30 prior evenings for eligibility). Label source columns: the target day's 16:00-22:00 MVA readings, plus the same substation's prior evening peaks; these are sealed (private label matrix) and never shipped in any solver-visible feature frame. The baseline operand (trailing p95) is computed from feature-side readings <= the instant and may ship as a numeric feature; the target evening readings cannot.

records.split_strategy: Temporal, by label year (year_end), computed from the actual audit_opinion_facts CSV (command: python3 candidates/za-municipal-audit-opinion/probe_label_stats.py <audit_opinions.csv>, scratch kept this session): train 2011-2017 = 1,863 rows / 878 positives (47.13%); eval 2018-2020 = 738 rows / 376 positives (50.95%); holdout 2021-2024 = 982 rows / 415 positives (42.26%). Both classes present in every one of the 14 label years (measured per-year rates 35.0%-56.5%). Clustered positives: audit outcomes correlate within an audit cycle/year, so the independence scale is ~14 label years, not 3,689 rows - confidence intervals must be clustered by year and the onset-conditioned variant recomputed at construction. Municipalities are repeated entities across years: features may include each municipality's own history, and the runner's id_columns handle the municipality code; no cross-split entity leakage arises because splits are by time, but the descriptor must declare expected duplicate ids.
records.target: Binary label from the audit_opinions cube ('Code' column, bulk CSV audit_opinion_facts on munimoney-media S3): 1 = qualified, disclaimer or adverse; 0 = unqualified or unqualified_emphasis_of_matter; 'outstanding' rows (audit not completed) are excluded, not imputed. Label source column is never shipped as a feature: the label CSV is used only to build y; features come from the separate incexp/cflow/capital/bsheet/grants/uifwexp/repmaint/aged-debtor/aged-creditor cubes and the demographics API. Measured per-year positive rates (qualified-or-worse, outstanding excluded): 35.0%-56.5% across all 14 label years, never degenerate. Measured persistence: 83.88% year-over-year agreement (2018-2020), so the level label is persistence-shaped and the primary task is the deterioration-onset conditioning; onset base rate measured 69/381 = 18.1% of clean-prev municipality-years in 2018-2020.

records.prediction_time: Instant = the announced embargo lift of the P0043.1 monthly release for reference month M (date+time published in advance by Stats SA; observed publication dates all fall in the last week of month M+1 at 14:30 SAST, lag 25-34 days after month end). At that instant, the latest published reference month is M; month M+1 is partially elapsed (the instant falls inside it), so M+1 can be neither feature nor target; the target month M+2 begins after the instant (about 4 days after) and ends about 34 days after it. Features are the released series values for months <= M only (current-vintage policy; see measurements.restatement_2026 and measurements.intra_basis_revisions). Dated example (Africa/Johannesburg): instant 2026-10-28 14:30 (embargo of the Release 2026-09 issue); feature window 2000-01..2026-09 as released in that vintage (first-available version = the monthly release; values for months M-11..M used by the label's trailing median are the values published at or before the instant); eligibility cutoff = series values for months <= 2026-09 exist; prediction instant 2026-10-28 14:30; target window 2026-11-01 through 2026-11-30 (starts 3 days 9.5 hours after the instant; ends 33 days 9.5 hours after). No part of the target window precedes the instant.

records.question: At the publication instant of the Stats SA P0043.1 'Statistics of liquidations' release for reference month M (published in the last week of month M+1, embargo lifting 14:30 SAST = 12:30 UTC; observed: 25 Mar 2026 for Feb issue, 27 May 2026 for Apr issue, 30 Sep 2026 14:30 for Aug issue, expected 28 Oct 2026 for Sep issue), will the number of liquidations in month M+2 for a given unit (companies/close-corporations x compulsory/voluntary x industry) exceed that unit's trailing 12-month median count over months M-11..M? Prospective users: credit and insurance exposure monitors, procurement/counterparty risk teams, and macro early-warning analysts, who get a ~1-month lead on industry-level insolvency pressure for provisioning and review decisions.
records.review: All five discovery contracts reconciled against recorded evidence. (1) Redistribution: class B - Stats SA permits applying, publishing and distributing the data with attribution, plus a no-sale condition our free releases satisfy (quoted in license_evidence; to be carried into LICENSE.md). (2) Prediction timing: instant = the announced embargo (measured on four issues; always last week of M+1 at 14:30 SAST), M+2 target window entirely after the instant; feature meanings documented by the publisher (export headers + release explanatory notes); vintage contract handled explicitly - the 2026 restatement is measured (110/110 months checked differ from the old basis), pre-restatement vintages are unrecoverable, so the task is a clearly-labelled current-vintage retrospective panel with no operational point-in-time claim for history; intra-basis revision tail measured (19/15,040, all recent months, +1..+7). (3) Target: derived from the published count series itself; label source column excludable by shipping lagged features only; recent-tail revisions noted. (4) Split capacity: measured - both classes in all three windows and all 26 years; independence scale is the month (~306 instants), within-month cross-unit dependence documented as the cluster. (5) Contribution: no ML-ready formulation of SA liquidation counts at any grain found in catalog or literature searches; nearest prior art is firm-level bankruptcy prediction (US/Italian firm panels), a different population and target; novelty check recorded by script. Residual uncertainty: future restatements of the same scale would change future basis (publisher warning observed and quoted); the construction must enforce a restricted prediction protocol against the abs-oad-style cross-row self-answer join (a row's label operand count(M+2) is a feature window value of the row whose target is M+4).

records.split_strategy: Temporal, by target month, computed from the fetched Release-2026-09 panel (command: python3 candidates/za-statsa-liquidations-exceedance/probe_base_rates.py, scratch 2026-10-27): population = 40 industry-level units (companies x compulsory/voluntary x 9 industries, close corporations x compulsory/voluntary x 9 industries) plus the 4 group totals; target month = reference month + 2 (M+2 frame). Median-exceedance label (trailing 12-month median > 0 filter): train target years 2002-2016 = 3,910 rows / 1,537 positives (39.3%), 30/40 units with positives; eval 2017-2020 = 992 / 426 (42.9%), 25/40; holdout 2021-2026 = 1,415 / 574 (40.6%), 24/40. YoY-direction label: train 4,748 / 1,980 (41.7%) 40/40 units, eval 1,206 / 568 (47.1%) 39/40, holdout 1,706 / 739 (43.3%) 39/40. Both classes present in every window and in every year 2001-2026 (positive months per year = 9-12 of 12). Clustering: the independence scale is the MONTH, not the row - 40 units share each month's macro shock, so ~306 scorable monthly instants over 26 years (2002-01..2026-09 minus warmup) are the effective sample; confidence intervals must be clustered by target month. No cross-split entity leakage: splits are by time; units repeat across months by design (panel task, runner id_columns carry the unit code).
records.target: Binary: count of liquidations for unit u in month M+2 (LIQ series value, 'Actual figures', number) > median of u's counts over months M-11..M (both operands from the same current-basis vintage; label source column = the unit's monthly count series itself, which is also the feature source - a row's shipped features are lagged values only, months <= M, never the target month's value). Alternative measured formulation: YoY direction (M+2 count > M-10 count). Trailing-median rows with median 0 (sparse series, all-zero window) are excluded as unlabelable; measured exclusion ~32% of unit-months under the 40-unit population.

packaged.prediction_time: The initial assessment instant, assessment_datetime, documented by the publisher as 'the date and time the wildfire was originally assessed by Alberta Wildfire employees'. Every feature field's meaning is documented at that instant: assessment_hectares, fire_spread_rate, fire_type, fire_position_on_slope, the five in-situ weather fields and fuel_type all carry the publisher's wording 'at the time of initial assessment'; reported_date/discovered_date/fire_start_date/detection fields are documented pre-instant and measured never to fall after the instant (27,828/27,828 for reported_date). Post-instant families are excluded by design and measurement: cause classification (dictionary: 'under investigation' temporary cause, final cause updated later), dispatch block (2.41% of dispatch timestamps fall after the assessment - mixed ordering, so excluded), all suppression/milestone fields (initial_action_by, ia_*, fire_fighting_start_*, bucketing, first_bh/uc/to/ex) and the label sources (current_size, size_class). Timestamps carry no timezone; they are read as local Alberta operational time (America/Edmonton) - a declared assumption to be confirmed at construction and stated in quality.json.evaluation_contract.

packaged.question: At Alberta Wildfire's recorded initial assessment of a newly discovered wildfire (assessment_datetime, 'originally assessed'), predict whether the wildfire will escape initial attack - final area burned at least 100 ha (variants at 4/40/200 ha) - and/or remain uncontained more than 72 hours (time from assessment to first under control), using only the crew-observed assessment record (size at assessment, rate of spread, fire behaviour type, position on slope, in-situ weather over the fire, FBP fuel type), pre-instant timing fields (estimated ignition, reported, detection channel), and calendar/geography. A useful prediction supports the actual initial-attack resourcing decision - airtanker/crew prioritization and same-day escalation - which the agency itself states happens at this instant.
packaged.review: All five discovery contracts reconciled against recorded evidence (probes and full transcripts in candidates/ab-wildfire-ia-escape/). (1) Redistribution: class A - OGL-Alberta v2.2 permits redistribution and derivatives; the attribution sentence and non-endorsement wording are recorded verbatim and carried into LICENSE.md; the personal-information exemption was checked against the shipped columns (position codes, not names). (2) Prediction timing: the instant is the publisher's own initial-assessment timestamp and every intended feature is documented 'at the time of initial assessment' by the publisher's dictionary - the strongest timing documentation of any source this bench has opened; post-instant families (cause, dispatch, suppression milestones) are excluded with measured ordering evidence; declared limitations: no timezone marker in timestamps (read as America/Edmonton, assumption to confirm) and a single current compilation (no historical per-fire vintages) - the task is labelled current-compilation retrospective, and evaluation_contract must state these assumptions plus the bounded revision-flip exposure (89 fires within +-20% of 100 ha). (3) Target: labels derive from the record's own post-instant fields (current_size, first_uc_date), excludable from shipped features; eligibility is assessment-based with 100% coverage - no outcome-conditioned selection; no censoring (terminal status on every row, 99.9% extinguished). (4) Split capacity: three disjoint year windows carry both classes for both labels (escape 1.86%/1.85%/4.11%; containment 3.2%/3.4%/9.8%), with same-day clustered counts recorded (independence scale = the extreme fire-weather day); the holdout's higher rate is the documented 2023 record season. (5) Not a mirror: the IA-escape family is precedented (WildfireIA US benchmark, Mesogeos, Zong et al. Alberta powerline subset, Korkola et al. Ontario, UAlberta IA-difficulty study) - none ships an all-cause, assessment-instant task on the regulator's own in-situ assessment observations with containment-milestone labels; WildfireIA's own abstract records that such 'response records' are non-public in the US, which is precisely the gap this source closes for a public jurisdiction. Novelty verdict 'differentiated' recorded by script. Residual uncertainties for construction: confirm the timezone reading against a publicly documented fire timeline; decide the already-controlled stratum's treatment for the containment label; winter/season scope decision.

packaged.split_strategy: Temporal, disjoint by the ASSESSMENT instant's calendar year (the time column; America/Edmonton local operational time): train 2006-2015 (15,864 fires), eval 2016-2020 (5,707), holdout 2021-2025 (6,257). 356 winter carryover fires assessed in the year after their record year move with their assessment; label-side counts are identical under the record-year rule (positives 297/104/257 = 1.87%/1.82%/4.11%; distinct positive assessment dates 156/79/128; containment>72h 514/189/611). Winter (Nov-Feb) rows kept and counted (587 total). The holdout escape rate is higher because 2021-2025 contains the 2023 record season - documented non-stationarity, recorded in quality.json limitations.
packaged.target: Primary label, binary: escape = final area burned (current_size, the publisher's 'final area burned of the wildfire') at or above the threshold (primary 100 ha; variants 4/40/200 ha measured). Secondary label, binary: containment = first under control (first_uc_date, 'sufficient suppression action to ensure no further spread') later than 72 hours after assessment_datetime; 42.0% of fires were already under control at the assessment instant (assessment == first_uc, a degenerate label-0 stratum the construction decision must handle and declare). Both labels derive entirely from the record's own post-instant fields; both source columns are excludable from what ships. Population: all wildfires in Alberta's Forest Protection Area, 2006-2025, one row per wildfire ((YEAR, FIRE_NUMBER) unique, measured); eligibility is assessment-based, not outcome-based (100% of discovered wildfires are assessed).

licence_summary.status: Two preserved upstream instruments, neither relicensed. CPCB CAAQM PM2.5 measurements: Government Open Data License - India (GODL-India v1.0) via the data.gov.in platform instrument, with its attribution template, non-endorsement, no-warranty and continuity conditions. The XKDR Forum Air-Quality-Database compilation carrying those measurements: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0, with the README's own requested credit. The redistributed fields are the publisher's own station identifiers, timestamps and hourly PM2.5 measurements (aggregated by us to daily statistics) plus our derived label, features and partition. The derived dataset is labelled as such throughout and is neither a CPCB product nor an XKDR Forum product.
