packaged.question: For a CPCB continuous ambient air-quality monitoring station in India, will the station's next-day (D+1) 24-hour mean PM2.5 concentration exceed 90 micrograms/m3 - the lower breakpoint of the CPCB National AQI 'Poor' band for 24-hour PM2.5 - given only that station's own hourly PM2.5 history through the end of day D?
packaged.review: Five contracts reconciled 2026-11-05 against recorded evidence. (1) REDISTRIBUTION - supported, class A: CPCB's own publication is licensed GODL-India by the data.gov.in platform instrument (Wayback-read 2026-11-04, AIKosh-corroborated live; attribution template + non-endorsement to carry into LICENSE.md; no share-alike); the XKDR compilation is CC BY 4.0 (README, credit 'India Air Quality Database, XKDR Forum' + CPCB + US DoS); OpenAQ is CC BY 4.0 (docs + archived v2 meta 'CC BY 4.0d'). (2) PREDICTION TIMING - supported for a clearly-labelled retrospective-research scope with two declared, unverified assumptions: instant = 23:59 IST on day D; features = the station's own trailing PM2.5 history through day D (naive IST, calendar-day convention); label = calendar-day D+1 24-hr mean, entirely after the instant. Assumption (a) current-vintage: the archive is one export (2026-09-30), values 'as reported', 'no gap filling', 'preliminary and not fully validated' (XKDR README) - no operational as-of claim; revision behaviour unmeasured (a second export has never been observed). Assumption (b) day-D trailing hours are treated as complete at the instant: CPCB intraday latency is not measured (the publisher's own 4 PM bulletin averages the past 24 h and shows non-participating stations, e.g. Delhi 36/39 on 2024-11-18). (3) TARGET - supported: mechanical label (D+1 calendar-day mean > 90 ug/m3) from a published band edge of the publisher's own AQI instrument (Poor band lower edge 91; quote in measurements.threshold_fixture_2026_11_05); label-source series excluded from every shipped column; known-event fixture bound to the publisher's Daily AQI Bulletin (2024-11-18 Delhi Severe 494) AND confirmed in the measured panel (36/36 complete Delhi station-days TRUE); the bulletin is also the publisher-summary cross-check (category-level). (4) SPLIT CAPACITY - supported, measured on the full 2019-2025 panel and re-cut once with measured evidence before any score (see split_strategy): train 2019-2022 63735 positives, eval 2023 20773 positives over 357 distinct positive days, holdout 2024 19254 positives over 358 days; both classes in all three windows; winter clustering recorded and cluster-aware evaluation required at construction. (5) NOT A MIRROR - supported: novelty_check verdict differentiated (2026-10-20): research papers fit CPCB forecasters with private splits (arXiv 2404.08702 22-station; Discover AI 2026), Kaggle raw-data mirrors (CC BY-SA), and open archives (OpenAQ/XKDR/Vayuayan) - none ships this task with fixed splits and a scored contract. RESIDUAL LIMITATIONS carried to construction: (i) the cross-row exposure - a scored day-D row's label operand (day D+1 mean) appears inside the trailing features of days D+2..D+91 - requires the za-cct-style bounded-exposure design (restricted trailing aggregates, isolated_rows declared, gate-1.5 reverse-history probes measuring eval/holdout coverage and mismatch); (ii) label-availability exclusions (station-days with <18 h on D+1) must be counted and declared, never silently dropped; (iii) the export's 2025 hole (Jan-Mar, Oct-Dec absent; the 2025-04..09 tail excluded) and the OpenAQ 2023-2024 gap (zero files, measured) mean XKDR is the only channel that carries all three re-cut windows; the full-key bulk path stays behind the operator's email/key decision while the anonymous measurements-API batching path remains viable and measured.

packaged.split_strategy: Temporal by day on the cpcb_caaqm stream only (5 us_embassy DS* stations excluded; one instrumentation stream). MEASURED 2026-11-06 by the accepted build cpcb-aqi-build-004 (single-pass fetch of the pinned XKDR export; the 2026-11-05 probe totals it replaces were defective - see measurements.attempt_002_refusal_2026_11_06): panel 717,429 station-days across 546 reporting stations (549 registered); windows train 2019-2022 339,756 / eval 2023 154,003 / holdout 2024 176,104 station-days; the 2025-04..09 partial tail 47,566 station-days / 829 valid-day positives is excluded and counted; the 2025-01..03 and 2025-10..12 hole months are asserted empty (0 rows). SHIPPED rows after eligibility (complete day D, labelable D+1): train 288,754 rows / 61,075 positives (21.15%) / 1,248 distinct positive days; eval 126,570 / 19,819 (15.66%) / 351; holdout 145,124 / 18,222 (12.56%) / 352. Excluded and counted per split: thin day D (33,586 / 18,065 / 20,101), unlabelable D+1 (17,416 / 9,368 / 10,879). Prevalence declines across the split (21.2% -> 15.7% -> 12.6%): an out-of-distribution property of the temporal split, reported rather than adjusted. Positives are winter-clustered (per-season eval prevalence DJF 33.0% vs JJAS 1.0%); construction evaluates with station-clustered intervals (cluster = station_id; 509 eval clusters). Both classes present in every window; eval/holdout clear the gate minimums with large margin.

packaged.split_strategy: Annual January instants with non-overlapping 12-month target windows. Proposed: train instants Jan 2016-2019 (targets 2016-2020), eval Jan 2020-2021 (targets 2020-2022), holdout Jan 2022-2024 (holdout target windows end by 2025-01, fully observed by the 2026-11-02 deactivated file). Instants 2011-2015 are usable for train with the pre-Oct-2014 no-ratings caveat; instants 2025+ are excluded while either the deactivated file's coverage or the publisher's migration-related cancellation lag is unresolved. Exact per-instant positives are the first construction measurement; measured anchor: T=2024-01-05 carries 14,765 eligible care homes and 758 positives (5.13%).
packaged.target: Binary: Location HSCA End Date in (T, T+365d]. Label source: CQC Deactivated Locations file (cumulative; Location HSCA End Date + Location Status; among care homes all-time: 17,046 Inactive-Dereg vs 131 Removed). Label-source columns never ship as features. Censoring: instants whose 12-month window extends past the deactivated file's coverage (2026-11-02 edition) are excluded. FRAMING: the target is the register event (deregistration of the location), which CQC notes can include services continuing under a new registration; not necessarily service cessation - see verdict.uncertainty.

packaged.split_strategy: Cohort split on advisory issue year (disjoint calendar-year windows, both classes in every window). Computed from the full fetched CSV (sha256 60f77ac4...) and cross-checked against independent SoQL aggregates run against the live API (identical numbers). Censored rows excluded from scored sets with per-window counts. Clustered (site-repeat) counts recorded because advisories cluster by site: 586 / 286 / 551 distinct sites per window.
packaged.target: Binary: advisory lifted within N days of issuance, N=30 primary (N=14 secondary; both base rates measured below). Label source columns: 'Date Advisory Removed' and 'Length of Advisory in Days' - label-only, excluded from shipped features. Publisher documents the censoring semantics on the dataset page: 'Values are not provided for boil advisories that are currently in effect.' (blank removal date = active). Scored rows require a removal date at the pinned vintage; censored rows are counted per window and excluded from scored sets, not treated as observed non-lifts.

licence_summary.status: No standard SPDX licence is declared; the operative instruments are the City of Cape Town Open Data Terms of Use (disclaimer-only: as-is, no warranty, no liability; no restriction on reuse, redistribution or derivatives for portal data) together with the Council-approved Open Data Policy 27781 ('freely used, shared and built-on by anyone, anywhere, for any purpose'), and the ArcGIS item's licenseInfo links the portal terms. The table is engineering telemetry (half-hourly apparent-power MVA readings per switching substation): no personal data, no third-party content, no official symbols. The redistributed fields are the publisher's own readings (timestamped MVA values and station identifiers) plus our derived binary label, at-instant aggregates, calendar fields and partition. The derived dataset is labelled as such throughout and is not a City of Cape Town product.

packaged.prediction_time: 06:00 Africa/Johannesburg (SAST, UTC+2) on day D, within the artifact's history. Features are the substation's half-hourly MVA readings with timestamps <= the instant (including day D's 00:00-06:00 readings), trailing aggregates computed only from readings <= the instant, plus calendar fields and substation identity. The evening target window 16:00-22:00 SAST lies entirely after the instant. packaged.publisher: City of Cape Town (Energy Directorate via the Corporate GIS Open Data Portal, odp-cctegis.opendata.arcgis.com) - metropolitan municipality in South Africa
packaged.question: For each City of Cape Town switching substation, at 06:00 SAST on day D, predict whether that substation's evening peak apparent-power load (maximum half-hourly MVA reading over 16:00-22:00 SAST on day D) will exceed the trailing-90-evening 95th percentile of its own evening peaks (evenings ending strictly before the instant).
packaged.review: All five discovery contracts are supported with measured evidence: class A licence from the publisher's own instruments; a within-artifact 06:00 SAST instant with a fully-post-instant evening target window and publisher-documented feature meaning (with the load-shift caveat recorded as a limitation); a label derivable from the same gapless table with sealable label-source columns; measured split capacity (train 2022 / eval 2023 / holdout 2024, 1,256-1,539 positives per year, clustered on 227-247 distinct days); and a differentiated novelty position (regression forecasting benchmarks exist on EU/US/AU substation data; none is African, none is a within-day exceedance classification with a sealed label contract). Honest labelling: retrospective_research - the closed 2022-2024 window was published as one table in 2026, so no historical-operational-availability claim is made and label timing is unverified outside the artifact's own timestamp order.

packaged.split_strategy: Temporal splits on station-days: train = 2022 (13,735 label-bearing station-days, 1,539 positives), eval = 2023 (14,965, 1,256), holdout = 2024 (15,006, 1,382). Disjoint years, both classes in every window, positives clustered on 227/246/247 distinct days per year. First ~30-90 evenings per station are burn-in (eligibility) and drop out of the labelled set. The evening-window 16:00-22:00 and the 06:00 instant are fixed for all splits; the sealed evening readings of any scored day never enter any shipped feature frame.
packaged.target: Binary: evening-peak exceedance. Label = (max half-hourly MVA over 16:00-22:00 SAST on day D for substation S) > (95th percentile of the same substation's evening peaks over the trailing 90 evenings ending strictly before the instant, minimum 30 prior evenings for eligibility). Label source columns: the target day's 16:00-22:00 MVA readings, plus the same substation's prior evening peaks; these are sealed (private label matrix) and never shipped in any solver-visible feature frame. The baseline operand (trailing p95) is computed from feature-side readings <= the instant and may ship as a numeric feature; the target evening readings cannot.

pending.question: At Alberta Wildfire's recorded initial assessment of a newly discovered wildfire (assessment_datetime, 'originally assessed'), predict whether the wildfire will escape initial attack - final area burned at least 100 ha (variants at 4/40/200 ha) - and/or remain uncontained more than 72 hours (time from assessment to first under control), using only the crew-observed assessment record (size at assessment, rate of spread, fire behaviour type, position on slope, in-situ weather over the fire, FBP fuel type), pre-instant timing fields (estimated ignition, reported, detection channel), and calendar/geography. A useful prediction supports the actual initial-attack resourcing decision - airtanker/crew prioritization and same-day escalation - which the agency itself states happens at this instant.
pending.review: All five discovery contracts reconciled against recorded evidence (probes and full transcripts in candidates/ab-wildfire-ia-escape/). (1) Redistribution: class A - OGL-Alberta v2.2 permits redistribution and derivatives; the attribution sentence and non-endorsement wording are recorded verbatim and carried into LICENSE.md; the personal-information exemption was checked against the shipped columns (position codes, not names). (2) Prediction timing: the instant is the publisher's own initial-assessment timestamp and every intended feature is documented 'at the time of initial assessment' by the publisher's dictionary - the strongest timing documentation of any source this bench has opened; post-instant families (cause, dispatch, suppression milestones) are excluded with measured ordering evidence; declared limitations: no timezone marker in timestamps (read as America/Edmonton, assumption to confirm) and a single current compilation (no historical per-fire vintages) - the task is labelled current-compilation retrospective, and evaluation_contract must state these assumptions plus the bounded revision-flip exposure (89 fires within +-20% of 100 ha). (3) Target: labels derive from the record's own post-instant fields (current_size, first_uc_date), excludable from shipped features; eligibility is assessment-based with 100% coverage - no outcome-conditioned selection; no censoring (terminal status on every row, 99.9% extinguished). (4) Split capacity: three disjoint year windows carry both classes for both labels (escape 1.86%/1.85%/4.11%; containment 3.2%/3.4%/9.8%), with same-day clustered counts recorded (independence scale = the extreme fire-weather day); the holdout's higher rate is the documented 2023 record season. (5) Not a mirror: the IA-escape family is precedented (WildfireIA US benchmark, Mesogeos, Zong et al. Alberta powerline subset, Korkola et al. Ontario, UAlberta IA-difficulty study) - none ships an all-cause, assessment-instant task on the regulator's own in-situ assessment observations with containment-milestone labels; WildfireIA's own abstract records that such 'response records' are non-public in the US, which is precisely the gap this source closes for a public jurisdiction. Novelty verdict 'differentiated' recorded by script. Residual uncertainties for construction: confirm the timezone reading against a publicly documented fire timeline; decide the already-controlled stratum's treatment for the containment label; winter/season scope decision.

pending.split_strategy: Temporal, disjoint by the ASSESSMENT instant's calendar year (the time column; America/Edmonton local operational time): train 2006-2015 (15,864 fires), eval 2016-2020 (5,707), holdout 2021-2025 (6,257). 356 winter carryover fires assessed in the year after their record year move with their assessment; label-side counts are identical under the record-year rule (positives 297/104/257 = 1.87%/1.82%/4.11%; distinct positive assessment dates 156/79/128; containment>72h 514/189/611). Winter (Nov-Feb) rows kept and counted (587 total). The holdout escape rate is higher because 2021-2025 contains the 2023 record season - documented non-stationarity, recorded in quality.json limitations.
pending.target: Primary label, binary: escape = final area burned (current_size, the publisher's 'final area burned of the wildfire') at or above the threshold (primary 100 ha; variants 4/40/200 ha measured). Secondary label, binary: containment = first under control (first_uc_date, 'sufficient suppression action to ensure no further spread') later than 72 hours after assessment_datetime; 42.0% of fires were already under control at the assessment instant (assessment == first_uc, a degenerate label-0 stratum the construction decision must handle and declare). Both labels derive entirely from the record's own post-instant fields; both source columns are excludable from what ships. Population: all wildfires in Alberta's Forest Protection Area, 2006-2025, one row per wildfire ((YEAR, FIRE_NUMBER) unique, measured); eligibility is assessment-based, not outcome-based (100% of discovered wildfires are assessed).

licence_summary.status: Two preserved upstream instruments, neither relicensed. CPCB CAAQM PM2.5 measurements: Government Open Data License - India (GODL-India v1.0) via the data.gov.in platform instrument, with its attribution template, non-endorsement, no-warranty and continuity conditions. The XKDR Forum Air-Quality-Database compilation carrying those measurements: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0, with the README's own requested credit. The redistributed fields are the publisher's own station identifiers, timestamps and hourly PM2.5 measurements (aggregated by us to daily statistics) plus our derived label, features and partition. The derived dataset is labelled as such throughout and is neither a CPCB product nor an XKDR Forum product.

pending.question: For a CPCB continuous ambient air-quality monitoring station in India, will the station's next-day (D+1) 24-hour mean PM2.5 concentration exceed 90 micrograms/m3 - the lower breakpoint of the CPCB National AQI 'Poor' band for 24-hour PM2.5 - given only that station's own hourly PM2.5 history through the end of day D?
pending.review: Five contracts reconciled 2026-11-05 against recorded evidence. (1) REDISTRIBUTION - supported, class A: CPCB's own publication is licensed GODL-India by the data.gov.in platform instrument (Wayback-read 2026-11-04, AIKosh-corroborated live; attribution template + non-endorsement to carry into LICENSE.md; no share-alike); the XKDR compilation is CC BY 4.0 (README, credit 'India Air Quality Database, XKDR Forum' + CPCB + US DoS); OpenAQ is CC BY 4.0 (docs + archived v2 meta 'CC BY 4.0d'). (2) PREDICTION TIMING - supported for a clearly-labelled retrospective-research scope with two declared, unverified assumptions: instant = 23:59 IST on day D; features = the station's own trailing PM2.5 history through day D (naive IST, calendar-day convention); label = calendar-day D+1 24-hr mean, entirely after the instant. Assumption (a) current-vintage: the archive is one export (2026-09-30), values 'as reported', 'no gap filling', 'preliminary and not fully validated' (XKDR README) - no operational as-of claim; revision behaviour unmeasured (a second export has never been observed). Assumption (b) day-D trailing hours are treated as complete at the instant: CPCB intraday latency is not measured (the publisher's own 4 PM bulletin averages the past 24 h and shows non-participating stations, e.g. Delhi 36/39 on 2024-11-18). (3) TARGET - supported: mechanical label (D+1 calendar-day mean > 90 ug/m3) from a published band edge of the publisher's own AQI instrument (Poor band lower edge 91; quote in measurements.threshold_fixture_2026_11_05); label-source series excluded from every shipped column; known-event fixture bound to the publisher's Daily AQI Bulletin (2024-11-18 Delhi Severe 494) AND confirmed in the measured panel (36/36 complete Delhi station-days TRUE); the bulletin is also the publisher-summary cross-check (category-level). (4) SPLIT CAPACITY - supported, measured on the full 2019-2025 panel and re-cut once with measured evidence before any score (see split_strategy): train 2019-2022 63735 positives, eval 2023 20773 positives over 357 distinct positive days, holdout 2024 19254 positives over 358 days; both classes in all three windows; winter clustering recorded and cluster-aware evaluation required at construction. (5) NOT A MIRROR - supported: novelty_check verdict differentiated (2026-10-20): research papers fit CPCB forecasters with private splits (arXiv 2404.08702 22-station; Discover AI 2026), Kaggle raw-data mirrors (CC BY-SA), and open archives (OpenAQ/XKDR/Vayuayan) - none ships this task with fixed splits and a scored contract. RESIDUAL LIMITATIONS carried to construction: (i) the cross-row exposure - a scored day-D row's label operand (day D+1 mean) appears inside the trailing features of days D+2..D+91 - requires the za-cct-style bounded-exposure design (restricted trailing aggregates, isolated_rows declared, gate-1.5 reverse-history probes measuring eval/holdout coverage and mismatch); (ii) label-availability exclusions (station-days with <18 h on D+1) must be counted and declared, never silently dropped; (iii) the export's 2025 hole (Jan-Mar, Oct-Dec absent; the 2025-04..09 tail excluded) and the OpenAQ 2023-2024 gap (zero files, measured) mean XKDR is the only channel that carries all three re-cut windows; the full-key bulk path stays behind the operator's email/key decision while the anonymous measurements-API batching path remains viable and measured.

The distinct-day counts are the clustered/independent-observation evidence for split capacity.
measurements.cross_check_publisher_summary: The publisher ships no summary product for this table (raw readings only; the ODP page carries only the description quoted above). The internal consistency check is the arithmetic identity rows = 48 x 1,096 and the gapless daily grid, both measured. No publisher aggregate exists to contradict.
measurements.dated_worked_example: Grassy Park 66kV, Africa/Johannesburg (SAST): day D = 2024-07-15 (Monday, mid-winter). Feature event window = half-hourly readings 2022-01-01 00:00 .. 2024-07-15 06:00 for this substation (trailing aggregates computed within it); prediction instant = 2024-07-15 06:00 SAST; eligibility = >= 30 prior evenings (met: 90 evenings 2024-04-16..2024-07-14 used); target window = 2024-07-15 16:00-22:00 SAST (entirely after the instant); measured label = evening peak 150.38 MVA > trailing-90-evening p95 146.82 MVA -> POSITIVE. Every target-window timestamp is later than the instant; no target-window reading can be a feature.
measurements.extraction_cost_measured: 53 HTTP GETs (1,000 rows/page, orderByFields=ObjectId, outFields all), 70,086,470 bytes JSON, 54.1 s wall clock on the coordinator (4 vCPU / 1.9 GiB class), measured 2026-11-01. No raw copy retained: the fetch streams to per-station-day aggregates only (probe_fullscan.py); reduced aggregates ~9 MB. Advancement-side construction must re-fetch on a worker and pin sha256.
measurements.novelty_scope_limitations: Web search (arXiv, HF, GitHub, Fraunhofer survey) 2026-11-01; queries recorded by scripts/check-novelty.py. The Fraunhofer 25-dataset public load-forecasting survey lists system/zone/substation datasets from EU/US/AU operators only; no African substation series surfaced. Hugging Face/Zenodo catalogue searches for this source's title returned no ML-ready formulation of this task.
measurements.panel_shape_measured: 52,608 rows = 48 half-hours x 1,096 days, 2022-01-01 00:00 .. 2024-12-31 23:30 SAST, gapless (0 days with !=48 half-hours). 45 fields: Timestamp + 43 substation columns (33kV/66kV/132kV switching stations) + ObjectId. 41 double-typed substation columns have 52,608/52,608 non-null values (ZERO nulls); Triangle_132kV (string-typed) contains no values at all; Morgen_Gronde_132kV (string-typed) carries numeric readings stored as strings (schema artifact: parse at construction or exclude; measured on fetch). 42 stations carry data in total (41 double + Morgen Gronde parsed), and all 41 double-typed stations are used for the measured label counts.
measurements.provenance_mix_measured: Single provenance stream: one reading per substation per half-hour from the City's SCADA/telemetry export; no sentinel/non-sentinel or multi-stream mixture. Two columns are string-typed (one empty, one numeric-as-text) - a schema artifact, not a separate population.
measurements.publisher_caveat: Item description (quoted): 'Users should note that readings are indicative of the measured Mega Volt-Ampere readings which have not been corrected for temporary load shifts due to operational requirements or load fluctuations due to load shedding.' The label therefore measures demand-as-dispatched, not underlying demand; this is documented meaning (usable), recorded as a limitation, and must appear in the dataset README.

measurements.seasonality_fixture: Known-event fixture (verified measured): Cape Town winter evening-peaking. Monthly mean evening peak over all stations: 2024-07 61.9 MVA vs 2024-12 44.1 MVA; same May-August rise in 2022 (2022-08 60.3 vs 2022-12 48.0) and 2023 (2023-07 60.6 vs 2023-12 45.9). Per-station winter(May-Aug)/summer(Nov-Feb) mean evening-peak ratios: Grassy Park 66kV 1.25, Atlantis Industrial 132kV 1.22, Foreshore 132kV (CBD) 0.98 - winter-peaking residential/industrial substations and a flat CBD profile, exactly as expected for Cape Town's winter-heating, summer-cooling-mild coastal climate.

Total 4,177/43,706. Both classes present in every year. Commands in notes.md (probe_fullscan.py, probe_cluster.py).

pending.split_strategy: Temporal splits on station-days: train = 2022 (13,735 label-bearing station-days, 1,539 positives), eval = 2023 (14,965, 1,256), holdout = 2024 (15,006, 1,382). Disjoint years, both classes in every window, positives clustered on 227/246/247 distinct days per year. First ~30-90 evenings per station are burn-in (eligibility) and drop out of the labelled set. The evening-window 16:00-22:00 and the 06:00 instant are fixed for all splits; the sealed evening readings of any scored day never enter any shipped feature frame.
pending.target: Binary: evening-peak exceedance. Label = (max half-hourly MVA over 16:00-22:00 SAST on day D for substation S) > (95th percentile of the same substation's evening peaks over the trailing 90 evenings ending strictly before the instant, minimum 30 prior evenings for eligibility). Label source columns: the target day's 16:00-22:00 MVA readings, plus the same substation's prior evening peaks; these are sealed (private label matrix) and never shipped in any solver-visible feature frame. The baseline operand (trailing p95) is computed from feature-side readings <= the instant and may ship as a numeric feature; the target evening readings cannot.
